issues.title: The night, and what the body learns in it
issues.category_name: Acute exposure: the bombardment itself, and the night it happens in
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Bombardment happens mostly at night, which means the damage is done to a nervous system that is supposed to be asleep. The body learns, within about three nights, that darkness is when it must be awake.

details.aspect: Sleep architecture goes first
details.description: Not insomnia in the ordinary sense. The person falls asleep and surfaces every forty minutes to check whether the sound was outside or inside the dream. Deep sleep is what stops, and deep sleep is where memory is filed.
details.energy_note: Tired in a way that sleeping does not fix.

details.aspect: The three-second identification problem
details.description: Everyone in a bombarded city becomes an amateur acoustician: outgoing or incoming, interceptor or impact, near or far. The skill is genuinely useful and it is also a permanent background process that never switches off.
details.energy_note: A part of the mind permanently assigned to listening.

details.aspect: Deciding about the basement, every time
details.description: Going down costs stairs, cold, other people and twenty minutes. Not going down costs nothing until the one time it does. It is a decision with no right answer and it is made several times a night.
details.energy_note: A coin flip you have to keep calling.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - Tehran, February to April 2026
details.description: Waves of strikes at all hours across a city of nearly ten million. The government texted residents to leave 'if possible while remaining calm'. Streets emptied, businesses shut, water and electricity facilities were damaged and people were asked to conserve.
details.energy_note: A whole city put on the same broken sleep schedule.
details.notes: Also: schools and universities closed by Supreme National Security Council directive.

details.aspect: The startle response outlives the war
details.description: Years later a door, a firework, a motorbike backfiring produces a full adrenal response in under 200 milliseconds - before any thought is possible. The person apologises for it, which does not stop it.
details.energy_note: Embarrassed by your own reflexes, in a safe country.
details.notes: Common report in chemical- and conventional-warfare survivor cohorts alike.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the fourth night
details.description: The first night they all went down. The second, most of them. By the fourth his mother refuses to move because the stairs hurt her knees more than the noise frightens her, and he sits on the landing between her and the door, which solves nothing and is the only thing he can do.
details.energy_note: Guarding a staircase against a missile.

details.aspect: It becomes the reference point for everything after
details.description: For the rest of the life, 'bad' is measured against that fortnight. Ordinary problems get scored as nothing, which sounds like resilience and is actually a calibration fault - real problems stop registering until they are large.
details.energy_note: Nothing else ever seems serious enough to deal with.

issues.title: Sirens, alerts, and the phone that decides your pulse
issues.category_name: Acute exposure: the bombardment itself, and the night it happens in
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Warning systems save lives and condition the population at the same time. The alert tone becomes a stimulus that produces a physical reaction independent of whether anything follows it.

details.aspect: Conditioning happens whether or not the threat lands
details.description: Ninety alerts of which two are real still produce ninety adrenal responses. The false alarms are not free; physiologically they cost the same.
details.energy_note: Paying full price for warnings about nothing.

details.aspect: Thirty seconds to shelter
details.description: In communities bordering Gaza the shelter window is thirty seconds or less. A population living under that clock was the group the Continuous Traumatic Stress Response scale was built and validated on.
details.energy_note: Half a minute, repeatedly, for years.

details.aspect: Clashing instructions from the people issuing them
details.description: During the 2026 strikes, Iranian, US and Israeli officials gave civilians contradictory directives about whether to stay or leave. Being told two incompatible things by authorities is itself a stressor: it removes the possibility of being correct.
details.energy_note: No available action is the right one.

details.aspect: The phone becomes the threat object
details.description: After the war the notification sound still produces the reaction. People silence their phones permanently, which then costs them work, appointments and relationships.
details.money_note: Missed work and opportunities from an unmonitored phone.
details.energy_note: Avoiding the device everyone else lives through.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - hypervigilance is expensive in ordinary life
details.description: Sustained threat monitoring consumes the same attention that would go to work, study and other people. The output drop is real and is usually attributed by employers to laziness.
details.energy_note: Judged for capacity that is already spent.

issues.title: The interruption of everything at once
issues.category_name: Acute exposure: the bombardment itself, and the night it happens in
issues.applies_to_note: Anyone physically present in a war zone
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: War does not damage one thing. School, work, transport, banking, medicine, post and the electricity that runs them all stop in the same week, so there is no functioning system left to fall back on.

details.aspect: Everything fails together, which is the point
details.description: Redundancy assumes independent failures. In war the failures are correlated by design, so every backup plan is disabled by the same event as the plan.
details.energy_note: No plan B, because B ran on the same grid.

details.aspect: Schools close and the year is gone
details.description: In the 2026 war, universities and schools were closed until further notice by directive. A closed school year is not recoverable time for a child; it is a permanent notch in a curve.
details.time_note: School days lost in one closure.
details.energy_note: A year removed from a childhood, quietly.
details.source_name: Supreme National Security Council directive, reported

details.aspect: Chronic medication stops being obtainable
details.description: Insulin, antipsychotics, anticoagulants, thyroid replacement. These are the drugs where a two-week gap is a medical event, and pharmacy supply is exactly what a strike or a blockade interrupts first.
details.money_note: Black-market or substitute pricing during shortage.
details.energy_note: Rationing your own tablets and doing the arithmetic nightly.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the diabetic grandmother
details.description: The clinic is shut, the pharmacy has queues down the block, and the insulin she has left is enough for nine days if she cuts the evening dose. She cuts the evening dose. Nobody records this anywhere as a war injury.
details.energy_note: A slow injury that will never be counted as one.

details.aspect: Income stops but obligations do not
details.description: Rent, loans and school fees carry on accruing through a period in which no work is possible. The debt created is a war injury that looks, on paper, like personal financial mismanagement.
details.energy_note: Arriving out of a war already behind.
details.notes: Cross-reference: assets/text/general excludes ordinary debt as not imposed. This is imposed, and the distinction matters.

issues.title: Decision-making under a threat that will not resolve
issues.category_name: Acute exposure: the bombardment itself, and the night it happens in
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Stay or go, now or tomorrow, this road or that one. The information needed to decide does not exist, the consequences are irreversible, and the decisions arrive faster than anyone can process them.

details.aspect: Irreversible choices made on no information
details.description: Leaving the house may be what saves the family or what kills it, and the difference is not knowable in advance. The choice still has to be made by a specific person at a specific hour.
details.energy_note: Responsibility without the means to be right.

details.aspect: Every outcome becomes retrospective evidence of your judgement
details.description: Whatever happens, the survivor treats it as proof of a decision they made. A neighbour's house hit becomes 'we were right'; their own becomes 'I should have known'. Neither inference is valid and both are made.
details.energy_note: Convicted by an outcome you did not control.

details.aspect: Decision fatigue in the technical sense
details.description: The capacity to make considered choices is finite and depletes. After a week of it, people make objectively worse decisions about objectively larger things, which is when the serious mistakes happen.
details.energy_note: Worst judgement exactly when it matters most.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - the habit of not deciding
details.description: Years later, ordinary choices - a job, a flat, a relationship - get deferred indefinitely, because the nervous system has learned that committing to a course of action is how people get hurt.
details.energy_note: A life put permanently on 'wait and see'.

issues.title: Leaving with what you can carry
issues.category_name: Displacement: leaving, and the shelter you leave for
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Displacement is usually described as a movement. Psychologically it is a forced triage of an entire life into one bag, performed in under an hour, with no possibility of revision.

details.aspect: The hour of sorting
details.description: Documents, medicine, money, one photograph. Everything that constitutes a family's evidence of itself either fits or does not. People report remembering what they left for the rest of their lives.
details.energy_note: A lifetime edited down in sixty minutes.

details.aspect: Documents are the difference between a person and a case number
details.description: A birth certificate, a deed, a degree. Without them the person abroad cannot prove they are who they say, owned what they owned, or studied what they studied, and no authority abroad will take their word for it.
details.money_note: Replacing or legalising documents from outside the country.
details.energy_note: Erased on paper while still alive.
details.notes: Links directly to assets/text/iran ADM and name-mismatch issues.

details.aspect: Repeat displacement compounds it
details.description: One move is a rupture. Seven is a condition. In Gaza, 95.3% of children in one displaced cohort had lost their homes and had experienced an average of nearly seven forced migrations.
details.energy_note: Unpacking stops being something you do.
details.source_name: Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Mental Health, 2026

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the bag that was wrong
details.description: He packed the laptop and the chargers, because he was thinking about work. Two years later in another country, he needs his grandfather's land deed and his mother's medical file, and both are in a drawer in a building that no longer stands.
details.energy_note: Punished for what you thought about under pressure.

details.aspect: Shelter is not safety, it is a different set of problems
details.description: Communal shelter removes privacy, sleep, sanitation and any control over who is near your children. The stress profile changes; it does not fall.
details.energy_note: Out of danger, into no walls at all.

details.aspect: The place you return to is not the place you left
details.description: Return is the stated goal for years. When it happens the street is different, the neighbours are gone, and the person discovers that the thing they wanted back was a time, not a location.
details.energy_note: Going home and finding it was never a place.

issues.title: The internal displacement nobody counts
issues.category_name: Displacement: leaving, and the shelter you leave for
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Most people displaced by war never cross a border. They move to a cousin's flat in another city, which involves no agency, no registration and no support, and puts two families under strain instead of one.

details.aspect: Hospitality has a half-life
details.description: The first fortnight is solidarity. By the second month the host family's own tolerance, money and space are gone, and nobody can say so out loud because of what is happening outside.
details.energy_note: A welcome you can feel expiring.

details.aspect: Children in a household that is not theirs
details.description: Different rules, no room, someone else's parents, and an instruction to be good because the family is a guest. Children respond with regression - bedwetting, clinging, silence - which the adults read as bad behaviour.
details.energy_note: Told to be perfect while the world is not.
details.notes: Regression under war stress is documented: 27% bedwetting reported by parents in Gaza during the Second Intifada, three quarters of children in the 2022 Save the Children survey.

details.aspect: No registration means no help and no record
details.description: Aid, compensation and later reparations follow lists. People who sheltered with relatives are on no list, so when anything is eventually distributed they are not eligible and cannot prove they were displaced at all.
details.money_note: Compensation never received because never registered.
details.energy_note: Displaced without being counted as displaced.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the eleven-month guest
details.description: Four adults and three children in a two-bedroom flat in Mashhad. He sleeps in the hallway. He has a job interview and no address he is willing to give.
details.energy_note: Employed nowhere, living in a corridor.

issues.title: Being unable to flee at all
issues.category_name: Displacement: leaving, and the shelter you leave for
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: The people who leave are the ones with money, documents, a car and somewhere to go. Everybody else stays, and knows precisely why they stayed.

details.aspect: Flight is a purchase
details.description: Fuel, a vehicle, a border fee, a bribe, a deposit somewhere else. Every one of those is a price, and the price rises exactly when demand does.
details.energy_note: Safety, sold at auction, during the auction.

details.aspect: The immobile are the old, the sick and their carers
details.description: Someone who cannot be moved anchors everyone who loves them. One bedridden parent immobilises a household of five, and everyone in it knows the arithmetic without saying it.
details.energy_note: Doing the maths on a person you love.

details.aspect: Staying is later reinterpreted as choosing
details.description: Those who left ask why you did not. Those who stayed ask why others did. Neither question has an answer that survives contact with the actual constraints, and both get asked for decades.
details.energy_note: Defending a decision that was never available.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - the guilt splits the family permanently
details.description: The brother who got out sends money and cannot visit. The brother who stayed receives it and cannot say what it costs him to. Twenty years later they are polite with each other.
details.energy_note: A family that works fine and is never close again.

issues.title: Death without a funeral
issues.category_name: Bereavement, the missing, and the body you never get back
issues.applies_to_note: Those who lost someone
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Grief in peacetime has a procedure: a body, a burial, a gathering, a period. War removes all four, and the mind does not process a loss it was never given the ritual for.

details.aspect: No body, no proof, no end
details.description: Without remains there is no moment at which the death becomes a fact. Part of the mind continues to run a search process, sometimes for decades.
details.energy_note: A door in your head that will not close.

details.aspect: Mass or hurried burial
details.description: Bodies buried quickly, collectively, or in the wrong place, under fire. The survivor carries not only the loss but the sense of having failed the dead in the one duty that was theirs.
details.energy_note: Failing someone who is already gone.

details.aspect: Ambiguous loss is its own category
details.description: 'Missing' is not a lighter version of 'dead'. It blocks grief, blocks inheritance, blocks remarriage, blocks the paperwork of a life, and keeps hope active at full strength indefinitely.
details.time_note: Often unresolved for the rest of the survivor's life.
details.energy_note: Hope, running continuously, as an injury.

details.aspect: The legal machinery makes it worse
details.description: Declaring someone dead in absentia takes years, requires evidence that does not exist, and asks the family to formally ask for it - to petition, in writing, for their own relative to be declared dead.
details.energy_note: Filing a form that kills your brother.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the phone that is still paid
details.description: Her son's number has been out of service for four years. She pays the line anyway, so that if it is ever switched on it will still be his.
details.money_note: Annual cost of a line kept live.
details.energy_note: A monthly direct debit as a form of prayer.

details.aspect: Anniversary reactions, permanently scheduled
details.description: The date arrives every year and produces a measurable physical response - sleep loss, appetite change, irritability - often before the person has consciously registered what day it is.
details.energy_note: Your body keeps the calendar for you.

issues.title: Losing several people at once
issues.category_name: Bereavement, the missing, and the body you never get back
issues.applies_to_note: Those who lost someone
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Bereavement services and the mind itself are built for one loss at a time. War delivers them in batches, and the second loss interrupts the processing of the first, and so on.

details.aspect: Grief queues and never clears
details.description: Each loss requires a period. When they arrive faster than the period, none of them are completed, and the person carries a stack of unfinished grief that presents clinically as depression rather than mourning.
details.energy_note: Mourning as a backlog.

details.aspect: Triage of feeling
details.description: Faced with four losses the mind picks one to feel and suppresses the rest. The suppressed ones surface years later, often at an unrelated funeral, with full original intensity.
details.energy_note: A grief that ambushes you at a stranger's service.

details.aspect: The survivor becomes the archive
details.description: When most of a family is gone, one person holds every name, recipe, story and grudge. It is a duty nobody assigned and it cannot be put down.
details.energy_note: Being the last person who remembers any of it.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the WhatsApp group
details.description: Eleven members. Four are dead. He cannot leave the group and cannot open it.
details.energy_note: An app you check and cannot read.

issues.title: Grieving from four thousand kilometres away
issues.category_name: Bereavement, the missing, and the body you never get back
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: Passports, visas, closed airspace, bans on movement
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Being abroad when someone dies at home removes every mechanism grief uses: the body, the house, the people, the food, the physical presence of others who also loved them.

details.aspect: The funeral happens on a video call
details.description: A phone held up at a graveside, with bad signal, for four minutes. That is the entire ritual, and afterwards the person goes to work.
details.energy_note: Burying your father on a screen, then answering email.

details.aspect: You cannot go, for reasons that are themselves the war
details.description: No visa, no flights, closed airspace, a warrant, a conscription record, or a reasonable fear of not being allowed out again. The inability to attend is produced by the same conflict as the death.
details.energy_note: Prevented from your own father's funeral by policy.
details.notes: Iranian airspace closures during 2026 and the visa bans under Proclamation 10998 both produce exactly this.

details.aspect: No one around you knows the dead person existed
details.description: Colleagues offer condolences for a name they have never heard, about a place they cannot picture, and then the week resumes. The loss has no social reality where the griever actually lives.
details.energy_note: Grief with no witnesses.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it fuses with the decision to emigrate
details.description: The death becomes retrospective evidence that leaving was a betrayal. This is not logical and it is close to universal.
details.energy_note: One death re-tries the whole life you chose.

issues.title: The blackout
issues.category_name: Information war: the blackout, the rumour, not knowing
issues.applies_to_note: Anyone physically present in a war zone
issues.war_form_note: Blackouts, jamming, propaganda, disinformation
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Resolves, given safety and time
issues.summary: Cutting a population's connectivity is a weapon used on both sides of a border at once: it isolates the people inside and it terrorises the people outside who cannot reach them.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - Iran, 2026
details.description: Connectivity fell nationwide within minutes of strikes on central Tehran. Starlink terminals were jammed and hundreds of suspected users detained. The blackout also made casualty figures and specific events difficult to verify from outside.
details.energy_note: A country switched off mid-sentence.
details.source_name: Al Jazeera; Fox News citing Israeli officials

details.aspect: Not knowing is worse than bad news, measurably
details.description: Uncertainty about whether a specific person is alive produces a stress response that does not habituate, because there is no information to adapt to. Confirmed bad news at least permits grief to start.
details.energy_note: The one state the mind cannot settle into.

details.aspect: Compulsive checking becomes the day
details.description: Refreshing a feed that does not update, re-sending a message that will not deliver, waiting for a check-in that does not come. Clinicians describe nocturnal monitoring of events as a defining diaspora symptom.
details.energy_note: A full-time job with no output.

details.aspect: Rumour fills the vacuum and is taken seriously
details.description: With no verifiable information, people act on the best available story. Families evacuate, spend money, and separate on the basis of a message forwarded six times.
details.energy_note: Life decisions made from a forwarded voice note.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the sister in Karaj
details.description: Last message: 'we're fine, going to my aunt's'. Sent Tuesday 19:12. It is now Sunday. He has read it about four hundred times and it says the same thing every time.
details.energy_note: Five days inside a single sentence.

details.aspect: Afterwards, the person does not trust information at all
details.description: Having lived through a period where official statements, rumour and silence were equally unreliable, the person applies that scepticism permanently - to doctors, employers and institutions in a country where it is unwarranted.
details.energy_note: Immune to being told the truth.

issues.title: Being lied to by everybody, on purpose
issues.category_name: Information war: the blackout, the rumour, not knowing
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Blackouts, jamming, propaganda, disinformation
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Every party to a modern conflict runs an information operation aimed at the civilian population. The effect on an individual is the removal of any reliable basis for deciding what to do.

details.aspect: Contradictory official instruction as a stressor
details.description: When the state, the attacker and foreign broadcasters each issue different advice on whether to stay or leave, the civilian is placed in a position where no compliance is possible.
details.energy_note: Obedience is not an option on offer.

details.aspect: Verification becomes unpaid labour
details.description: Hours per day spent cross-checking claims across channels in two or three languages, performed by people who also have to eat and sleep.
details.energy_note: A second job as your own intelligence analyst.

details.aspect: The epistemic damage lasts
details.description: Chronic exposure to coordinated deception produces durable cynicism. It protects against propaganda and also against public health advice, legal rights information and anything else that arrives through an institution.
details.energy_note: Armoured against the truth as well.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it isolates you from people who were not there
details.description: Explaining to a colleague why you do not believe a government press release makes you sound paranoid. So you stop explaining, which is the isolation.
details.energy_note: Sane, and unable to sound it.

issues.title: Watching your own city on a stranger's timeline
issues.category_name: Information war: the blackout, the rumour, not knowing
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: Blackouts, jamming, propaganda, disinformation
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the next generation through silence, story, ritual and community
issues.summary: The war arrives as an infinite feed of graphic content about specific streets the viewer knows, interleaved with advertising and other people's holidays.

details.aspect: Digital media as amplifier
details.description: Continuous immersion in graphic content and live updates extends the reach of the violence, makes disengagement difficult, and can trigger anxiety, depression and PTSD-like symptoms in people who are physically safe.
details.energy_note: Injured by a device you are holding voluntarily.

details.aspect: Recognising the geography is what does the damage
details.description: A generic war video is distressing. A video of the junction where you bought bread for eleven years is something else, and the algorithm cannot tell the difference so it serves more of it.
details.energy_note: The feed learns exactly which street to show you.

details.aspect: Parallel realities
details.description: Outward normality - meetings, school runs, small talk - running at the same time as worry, grief and anger, with no overlap between the two. Clinicians name this directly in the diaspora literature.
details.energy_note: Two lives, neither of them fully attended.

details.aspect: You cannot look away because looking is the only participation available
details.description: Putting the phone down feels like abandonment. So the person keeps watching, knowing it helps nobody, because stopping would mean accepting that nothing they do helps anybody.
details.energy_note: Doomscrolling as a form of loyalty.

issues.title: PTSD, as it actually presents
issues.category_name: Post-traumatic stress, and the kind that has no 'post'
issues.applies_to_note: Anyone physically present in a war zone
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: The diagnosis is well known and the presentation is not. It is mostly not flashbacks; it is sleep, irritability, concentration, numbness, and an avoidance pattern the person has rationalised so thoroughly they no longer notices it.

details.aspect: Prevalence in exposed child populations is not marginal
details.description: 57.8% of displaced Gazan children screened positive for PTSD on CATS cutoffs, 15.6% meeting the stricter DSM-5 algorithm; pooled estimates from earlier Palestinian child studies put it at 36%, and Syrian refugee children at 30-50%. After the November 2012 war, 53.5% of 1,029 pupils aged 11-17 met DSM-V criteria.
details.energy_note: A majority of a generation, not an unlucky minority.
details.source_name: Child Adolesc Psychiatry Ment Health 2026; PMC7137754

details.aspect: Avoidance is the part that wrecks the life
details.description: Not the nightmares. The systematic, invisible narrowing of where the person will go, what they will watch, who they will talk to and what subjects are permitted - each avoidance individually reasonable, collectively a cage.
details.energy_note: A life that gets smaller by one room a year.

details.aspect: Concentration loss reads as incompetence
details.description: Intrusive material consumes working memory. The result looks like someone who cannot follow a meeting or finish a document, and is appraised as such by managers who have no idea.
details.money_note: Lost earnings and promotions over a career.
details.energy_note: Demoted for an injury nobody can see.

details.aspect: Irritability costs the relationships that would have helped
details.description: The anger is disproportionate, the person knows it is disproportionate, and knowing does not prevent it. The people who leave because of it are usually the ones who were the support.
details.energy_note: Driving off the people who were holding you up.

details.aspect: Complex PTSD is common where the exposure was prolonged
details.description: Recent Gaza research reports alarmingly high rates of both PTSD and complex PTSD, with emotional regulation, identity and relational functioning affected rather than just fear responses.
details.energy_note: Not a fear problem. A self problem.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - the cost is paid over forty years, in instalments
details.description: Reduced earnings, earlier exit from work, higher medical utilisation, more relationship breakdowns. None of it is invoiced to the war.
details.money_note: Rough lifetime economic cost, individual.
details.energy_note: A bill that arrives monthly for four decades.

issues.title: Continuous traumatic stress: when there is no 'post'
issues.category_name: Post-traumatic stress, and the kind that has no 'post'
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: PTSD assumes the trauma has ended. For a population under ongoing or recurring threat it has not, which makes hypervigilance a correct assessment of reality rather than a symptom to be treated.

details.aspect: The concept and where it came from
details.description: Developed in the 1980s by mental health professionals in apartheid-era South Africa, who found PTSD frameworks failed people whose victimisation was ongoing rather than finished.
details.energy_note: A diagnosis written for a war that ended.
details.source_name: Straker et al.; APA special issue 2013

details.aspect: The symptoms are adaptive, which is why treating them fails
details.description: Avoiding the street during shelling and not sleeping during an air raid are correct responses. Evidence: once a resident leaves the affected area, symptoms subside dramatically - the opposite of a conditioned false alarm.
details.energy_note: Being told to relax about something that is still happening.
details.source_name: PTSD under ongoing threat review, PMC4980518

details.aspect: Its factor structure is different from PTSD
details.description: The validated Continuous Traumatic Stress Response scale loads on exhaustion/detachment, rage/betrayal and fear/helplessness - not intrusion, avoidance and arousal. Rage and betrayal are the ones clinicians miss.
details.energy_note: It comes out as fury at your own government, not fear.

details.aspect: It escalates rather than habituating
details.description: Consistent with allostatic load: repeated attacks reinforce the belief that the threat will never end, and wellbeing erodes over time. Inadequate response by authorities specifically fosters rage and helplessness.
details.energy_note: It gets worse with practice, not better.

details.aspect: No DSM-5 or ICD-11 status, which has practical consequences
details.description: Because it is a framework rather than a diagnosis, it cannot be claimed for, insured against, or used to obtain accommodations at work or in asylum proceedings.
details.money_note: Treatment and claims not covered because the condition is not coded.
details.energy_note: Real, documented, and not on any form.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the ceasefire that changed nothing
details.description: The conditional ceasefire was declared in April. He still does not sleep, because a conditional ceasefire is a description of the present, not a promise about the future, and his body has read the word 'conditional'.
details.energy_note: Peace, subject to terms, is not peace to a nervous system.

issues.title: The body keeps the bill: physical health after war stress
issues.category_name: Post-traumatic stress, and the kind that has no 'post'
issues.applies_to_note: Anyone physically present in a war zone
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up fifteen to forty years later, or in the next generation
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Chronic threat exposure is not confined to the mind. It shows up as cardiovascular disease, metabolic change, immune dysfunction and pain, on a delay of ten to thirty years.

details.aspect: Somatic presentation is the norm, not an alternative
details.description: In the 2026 Halabja study, severe somatic symptoms accompanied 79% PTSD and 65% depression/anxiety rates. The lead researcher noted headaches, back pain and exhaustion often express psychological wounds directly.
details.energy_note: The pain is real and the cause is not in the joint.

details.aspect: Which means years of the wrong investigations
details.description: The patient presents with chest pain and gets a cardiac workup. Then a gastric one. Then a neurological one. Each is negative, each costs money and months, and each reinforces the sense of not being believed.
details.energy_note: Investigated repeatedly and told there is nothing wrong.

details.aspect: HPA-axis dysregulation is the common mechanism
details.description: Sustained glucocorticoid signalling changes - the same system implicated in FKBP5 and NR3C1 findings in survivor cohorts - link the psychological to the metabolic and immune.
details.energy_note: One broken thermostat, wired to everything.
details.source_name: Yehuda et al., Biological Psychiatry 2015 / AJP 2020

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it lands in the decade you were going to earn in
details.description: The cardiac event at 52, the disability at 57. The years removed are the peak-earning, pension-building ones, so the financial consequence is disproportionate to the medical one.
details.energy_note: The war collects in your fifties.

issues.title: Not being able to describe it, in any language
issues.category_name: Post-traumatic stress, and the kind that has no 'post'
issues.applies_to_note: Anyone physically present in a war zone
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Recovery frameworks are built on the assumption that the experience can be narrated. A large part of war exposure is encoded as sensation, not story, and the person has no words for it in their first language, let alone their third.

details.aspect: Therapy is a language-intensive activity
details.description: Processing a trauma in a second language, through an interpreter, in fifty minutes, to a clinician with no context for the place or the war. It can work. It works less well and costs more.
details.money_note: Sessions, often uncovered, often needing more of them.
details.energy_note: Explaining your worst night with a limited vocabulary.

details.aspect: The smell is the part that has no word
details.description: Olfactory memory bypasses language entirely and is the most reliable trigger reported by survivors of both blast and chemical exposure. There is no way to describe it to a therapist and no way to avoid it in a city.
details.energy_note: Ambushed by a smell in a supermarket.

details.aspect: Alexithymia after prolonged threat
details.description: Extended numbing removes access to the person's own emotional state. Asked how they feel, the honest answer is that they do not know, and that answer is often read as resistance.
details.energy_note: Asked a question about yourself that you cannot answer.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the intake form
details.description: Question 9: 'Describe the traumatic event.' There are four lines. He writes 'war' and puts the pen down.
details.energy_note: Four lines for eight years.

issues.title: Survivor guilt, in its specific forms
issues.category_name: Moral injury, guilt, and the ones who lived
issues.applies_to_note: Anyone physically present in a war zone
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Not a vague sadness. A set of concrete, recurring propositions - I took the seat, I did not go back, I was asleep - each of which the person has examined thousands of times and cannot dismiss.

details.aspect: It attaches to specific acts, which is what makes it durable
details.description: General guilt fades. 'I took the last seat in the car' does not, because it is true, and no amount of reframing makes it untrue.
details.energy_note: A fact about yourself you cannot argue with.

details.aspect: Guilt for the freedoms you now have
details.description: Named directly in diaspora clinical writing: guilt for the safety you enjoy, intensified by the belief that you are not doing enough, until the privilege of being safe becomes too heavy to carry.
details.energy_note: Safety as a thing you owe money on.

details.aspect: Self-punishment presents as bad decisions
details.description: Sabotaging a promotion, ending a good relationship, refusing treatment. The mechanism is a felt conviction that comfort is not permitted, and it is almost never articulated as that.
details.money_note: Career and relationship costs of unrecognised self-sabotage.
details.energy_note: Quietly declining a life you think you have not earned.

details.aspect: It cannot be relieved by the people it concerns
details.description: The dead cannot absolve. The survivors in the country say 'don't be silly', which does not land. There is no one with standing to grant the pardon.
details.energy_note: A debt with no creditor to pay.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it converts into overwork
details.description: Justifying the survival through achievement. Effective for a decade, then it collapses, usually as burnout, usually diagnosed as depression with no reference to the war at all.
details.energy_note: Twelve productive years and a wall at the end of them.

issues.title: Moral injury: doing, or failing to do
issues.category_name: Moral injury, guilt, and the ones who lived
issues.applies_to_note: Anyone physically present in a war zone
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Distinct from fear-based trauma. Moral injury is the damage from having acted, or failed to act, against one's own code - and it responds poorly to treatments designed for fear.

details.aspect: The choices that cause it are usually forced ones
details.description: Which child to carry. Whether to open the door. Whether to give the name. These are not moral failures; they are impossible positions. The injury happens anyway.
details.energy_note: Judged by yourself, under rules that did not apply.

details.aspect: Exposure therapy is the wrong tool
details.description: Fear extinguishes with repeated safe exposure. Guilt and shame do not; repeating the memory without addressing the moral content can deepen them.
details.money_note: Cost of treatment that does not work first.
details.energy_note: Correctly referred, wrongly treated.

details.aspect: It attacks the identity rather than the nervous system
details.description: The conclusion is not 'the world is dangerous' but 'I am a certain kind of person'. That is not a symptom that medication reaches.
details.energy_note: A verdict, not an alarm.

details.aspect: Conscripts carry it without having chosen any of it
details.description: Compulsory service means the acts were performed by someone who did not choose the war, the unit, the order or the year. The moral weight lands on them regardless.
details.energy_note: Conscripted into something you will answer for alone.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the checkpoint
details.description: He was nineteen and he was told to keep the queue moving. He kept the queue moving. He is fifty-four and he has never told his wife about the woman with the blue bag, and he could not now say what he thinks he did wrong.
details.energy_note: Thirty-five years of an unexamined three seconds.

issues.title: Rage at your own side
issues.category_name: Moral injury, guilt, and the ones who lived
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: One of the least discussed effects. Civilians under bombardment frequently direct their strongest anger not at the attacker but at their own authorities, for the shelter that was not built and the warning that did not come.

details.aspect: It is in the instrument
details.description: Rage and betrayal is one of the three factors in the validated CTSR scale, alongside exhaustion/detachment and fear/helplessness. Inadequate response by authorities is specifically identified as what generates it.
details.energy_note: The anger has a domestic address.

details.aspect: It cannot be expressed where it would be dangerous to
details.description: In a state with functioning security services the anger has nowhere to go, so it turns inward or onto the family. Suppressed political rage is one of the commonest routes from war stress to domestic violence.
details.energy_note: Anger that can only be spent at home.

details.aspect: Abroad, it is misread as support for the enemy
details.description: The refugee who criticises their own government is assumed to endorse the people who bombed them. The refugee who does not is assumed to be a regime loyalist. There is no available position.
details.energy_note: Two wrong boxes and no third one.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it forecloses the diaspora politics that might have helped
details.description: Communities fracture along these lines instead of organising, which removes the collective action that the literature identifies as the main protective factor available to people abroad.
details.energy_note: The one thing that helps, made impossible.

issues.title: Development does not pause for the war
issues.category_name: Children: development, school, and the years that do not come back
issues.applies_to_note: Children and adolescents, whose development is running while it happens
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: An adult loses time. A child loses a stage. Language, attachment, literacy and social learning run on windows, and a window missed is not reopened by the conflict ending.

details.aspect: Regression is the standard response and is read as misbehaviour
details.description: Bedwetting, clinging, loss of acquired speech, return to baby talk. Save the Children found three quarters of Gazan children bedwetting in fear in 2022, with a growing number showing reactive mutism.
details.energy_note: Punished for going backwards under a bombardment.

details.aspect: The Second Intifada numbers, for the same picture twenty years earlier
details.description: Mousa and Madi 2003: 46% of parents reported aggression in their children, 38% worse school results, 27% bedwetting, 39% nightmares.
details.energy_note: The same four symptoms, every war, every decade.

details.aspect: Nightmares at industrial scale
details.description: 56% of Gazan 10-12 year olds reported recurrent nightmares, averaging 4.2 nights a week with a mean duration of about 2.5 years. In the Better Learning Programme cohort of 1,093 children, the average was 4.86 nights a week before treatment.
details.time_note: Mean duration ~2.5 years of recurrent nightmares.
details.energy_note: Two and a half years of being afraid to go to sleep.

details.aspect: Attachment disruption, because the parent is not available
details.description: A terrified or grieving parent cannot provide the regulation an infant needs. The child's stress system is calibrated in that period, and it is calibrated to the parent's state, not the bombs.
details.energy_note: The war reaches the baby through the mother's face.

details.aspect: Schooling loss compounds mechanically
details.description: A systematic review of 83 studies shows children exposed to recurrent or severe trauma are at significant risk of cognitive impairment, social-emotional-behavioural problems and academic difficulty - on top of the days simply not attended.
details.money_note: Lifetime earnings effect of lost schooling years.
details.energy_note: The gap widens by itself for the next ten years.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - the diagnosis arrives in the destination country, wrongly
details.description: Resettled children present as inattentive, oppositional or delayed and are assessed by systems with no trauma-informed context and often no shared language. Misdiagnosis in both directions is routine.
details.energy_note: Labelled for life by a fifty-minute assessment.

issues.title: Growing up with a parent who is not fully present
issues.category_name: Children: development, school, and the years that do not come back
issues.applies_to_note: Children and adolescents, whose development is running while it happens
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Outlives the person it started in
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the child through how the parent is able to parent
issues.summary: The child of a war-injured parent is not a bystander. Parental PTSD changes the emotional climate of the household every day for the whole of a childhood.

details.aspect: Unpredictability is the mechanism
details.description: Not cruelty. A parent who is warm on Tuesday and unreachable on Wednesday teaches a child that safety is not stable, which is the same lesson the war taught the parent.
details.energy_note: Learning the same thing without the war.

details.aspect: Role reversal - the child manages the parent
details.description: Children of traumatised parents commonly take on monitoring: reading the mood, managing siblings, keeping the house quiet. It produces capable adults who cannot rest.
details.energy_note: Competent at nine, exhausted at forty.

details.aspect: The silence is transmitted too
details.description: Families frequently decide not to tell the children. The children grow up sensing a large unspecified thing, and often construct a worse version of it than the truth.
details.energy_note: A secret they can feel the shape of.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the noise rule
details.description: No shouting in the house. No doors. No fireworks at new year, ever. He learned these before he learned why, and he keeps them now, in a house of his own, in a country his father never saw.
details.energy_note: Enforcing a dead man's air-raid rules in Toronto.

details.aspect: It is not deterministic, and saying so matters
details.description: The Halabja three-generation study and the Holocaust literature both find elevated risk, not certainty. Many descendants are fine. The dataset records elevated probability, not a verdict on any individual.
details.energy_note: Higher odds. Not a sentence.

issues.title: Children with no schooling system to return to
issues.category_name: Children: development, school, and the years that do not come back
issues.applies_to_note: Children and adolescents, whose development is running while it happens
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: The institutions are not merely closed. Teachers are displaced or dead, buildings are rubble or shelter, records are destroyed, and the qualification a child needs proof of has no issuing authority left.

details.aspect: Attention in the classroom is gone even when it reopens
details.description: After the 2014 war, UNRWA teachers reported students falling asleep in class, unable to concentrate, and performing poorly. The building being open is not the same as education happening in it.
details.energy_note: Present, seated, and not learning anything.

details.aspect: Missing transcripts follow a person for thirty years
details.description: A destroyed school archive means no certificate, which means no university abroad, which means a career ceiling set by an administrative event in a war the person was eight years old for.
details.money_note: Re-sitting exams, equivalency assessments, lost years.
details.energy_note: Your qualifications were in a building.
details.notes: Directly compounds the credential-recognition hurdles in assets/text/iran.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the equivalency board
details.description: They want the original stamped transcript. The school was destroyed in 2015 and the ministry that held the duplicate was destroyed in 2016. The board notes that without documentation it cannot proceed, and closes the file.
details.energy_note: A file closed because a country was.

details.aspect: Interrupted-schooling children are placed by age, not level
details.description: A fourteen-year-old with four years of schooling goes into a class with fourteen-year-olds. The gap is never closed and the child correctly concludes they are stupid.
details.energy_note: Taught daily that you cannot do it.

issues.title: Play, and what replaces it
issues.category_name: Children: development, school, and the years that do not come back
issues.applies_to_note: Children and adolescents, whose development is running while it happens
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Children process the unmanageable through play, and under war the play becomes re-enactment: checkpoints, funerals, bombing. Adults find it disturbing and stop it, which removes the only processing mechanism the child has.

details.aspect: Post-traumatic play is repetitive and joyless
details.description: Ordinary play is generative. Post-traumatic play repeats the same sequence without resolution, which is diagnostic, and which adults reliably misinterpret as morbid interest.
details.energy_note: A game that never gets to the end.

details.aspect: Nowhere to do it
details.description: Play needs space, other children, and a level of adult inattention that is not available in a shelter. Removing the space removes the mechanism.
details.energy_note: No corner of the world left that is theirs.

details.aspect: Where it is used deliberately it works
details.description: The school-based Better Learning Programme treated 1,093 war-exposed students in over 100 Gaza schools; roughly half reported no nightmares after treatment and a further 47% reported reduced frequency.
details.energy_note: Cheap, school-based, and it actually worked.
details.notes: One of the few unambiguously positive findings in this dataset.

details.aspect: Adolescents get no equivalent at all
details.description: Programmes target under-twelves. Adolescents, who are simultaneously processing the war and forming an identity in it, are largely unserved, and are the group that goes on to fight in the next one.
details.energy_note: The age nobody builds a programme for.

issues.title: Prenatal stress and neurodevelopmental risk
issues.category_name: Neurodevelopment: what war does before birth
issues.applies_to_note: Those exposed in utero, or conceived after
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up fifteen to forty years later, or in the next generation
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.transmission_note: Exposed before birth, through the mother's physiology
issues.summary: Exposure begins before birth. Maternal stress during pregnancy is associated with elevated risk of ASD and ADHD in the offspring - elevated, not determined, and the distinction is the whole of the honest version.

details.aspect: The meta-analytic numbers
details.description: A 2019 systematic review and meta-analysis found prenatal stress associated with ASD at pooled OR 1.64 (95% CI 1.15-2.34, 15 studies) and ADHD at OR 1.72 (95% CI 1.27-2.34, 12 studies). Heterogeneity was very high - I-squared 90% and 85% - which is a real caveat, not a footnote.
details.energy_note: Risk up by roughly two thirds. Not a cause.

details.aspect: The largest trauma-specific cohort
details.description: A Swedish register study of 553,766 children born 2006-2010 found prenatal maternal PTSD associated with offspring ADHD at crude OR 1.79 (1.37-2.34). Importantly, in children with indicators of heredity the association was partly explained by it - genetic confounding accounts for some of it.
details.energy_note: Partly the war, partly the family. Both are true.

details.aspect: There is a window
details.description: The placenta modulates fetal exposure to maternal glucocorticoids, but becomes less protective near the end of mid-gestation - roughly weeks 19 to 26 in humans - leaving the fetus more exposed at that point.
details.energy_note: A two-month window, and a war does not check the calendar.

details.aspect: Male-biased effects are reported repeatedly
details.description: Van den Bergh & Marcoen found prenatal stress associated with markedly more ADHD symptoms in boys than girls; a severe-earthquake prenatal cohort found increased depression rates only in males.
details.energy_note: Sons take more of it, for reasons not yet settled.

details.aspect: What this costs a family over a lifetime
details.description: Assessment, therapy, specialist schooling, a parent leaving work, and adult support. Most of it is paid by the household, in a country that may not recognise the diagnosis, in a language the parents do not fully have.
details.energy_note: A bill that starts at age three and does not stop.

details.aspect: HONEST LIMIT - this is association, and the mechanism is not settled
details.description: Proposed mechanisms are DNA methylation and HPA-axis programming, with placental inflammatory and nutrient-sensing pathways implicated. None of this licenses telling any individual family that the war caused their child's autism. The dataset records elevated population risk.
details.energy_note: What is known, and firmly where it stops.

issues.title: Famine and deprivation in utero
issues.category_name: Neurodevelopment: what war does before birth
issues.applies_to_note: Those exposed in utero, or conceived after
issues.war_form_note: Encirclement, blockade, deliberate deprivation
issues.onset_note: Shows up fifteen to forty years later, or in the next generation
issues.duration_note: Outlives the person it started in
issues.transmission_note: Exposed before birth, through the mother's physiology
issues.summary: Siege and blockade produce maternal malnutrition, and the best-documented prenatal exposure in all of human epidemiology is a famine caused by a war.

details.aspect: The Dutch Hunger Winter, 1944-45
details.description: Individuals exposed periconceptionally showed less methylation of the imprinted IGF2 gene six decades later than their own unexposed same-sex siblings. Exposure at the end of pregnancy produced no such difference - the timing is the finding.
details.energy_note: A mark still readable sixty years later.

details.aspect: The psychiatric outcome
details.description: Prenatal famine exposure is associated with increased risk of schizophrenia and depression in adulthood. Meta-analysis confirms the schizophrenia association; the mediating methylation signal identified is DUSP22, not IGF2 - IGF2 tracks growth and metabolism instead.
details.energy_note: A psychiatric illness scheduled before birth.

details.aspect: Genome-scale work replaced the candidate-gene story
details.description: Malnutrition-associated differentially methylated regions preferentially occur at regulatory regions and map to genes differentially expressed in early development; DMRs in INSR and CPT1A showed enhancer activity and tracked birth weight and LDL cholesterol.
details.energy_note: Not one gene. A setting across a pathway.

details.aspect: It is being applied to current sieges
details.description: Published work now extends the famine-epigenetics framework explicitly to maternal malnutrition in Gaza, on the expectation of the same class of outcome in a cohort currently in utero.
details.energy_note: A cohort being created now, measurable in 2080.
details.source_name: ScienceDirect, maternal malnutrition and epigenetics in Gaza

details.aspect: HONEST LIMIT - the grandchildren claim is not established
details.description: Heijmans 2008 measured only the directly exposed generation. Assertions that IGF2 methylation changes are inherited into F2 and F3 are extrapolations, not findings. Human transgenerational epigenetic inheritance remains largely unproven.
details.energy_note: Where the evidence actually stops.

issues.title: Blast, toxicants and the developing brain
issues.category_name: Neurodevelopment: what war does before birth
issues.applies_to_note: Children and adolescents, whose development is running while it happens
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Beyond stress: war deposits heavy metals, combustion products and munition residues into the air, water and soil that a child is growing in.

details.aspect: Rubble is not inert
details.description: Pulverised concrete, asbestos from older buildings, lead from paint and pipes, and combustion products, inhaled by children playing in it for years after the fighting.
details.energy_note: A playground made of the building.

details.aspect: Lead exposure and neurodevelopment is not controversial
details.description: Unlike the prenatal-stress literature, the developmental effect of lead on IQ and attention is settled science. War reliably remobilises lead that was safely bound in structures.
details.energy_note: The least disputed mechanism in this whole file.

details.aspect: Nobody measures it, so nobody can claim for it
details.description: Environmental sampling requires a functioning state, which is precisely what is absent. Twenty years later there is no baseline data and therefore no basis for any compensation claim.
details.energy_note: Unmeasured, therefore never happened.

details.aspect: Water and sanitation failure has its own developmental cost
details.description: Repeated early-childhood diarrhoeal illness and chronic undernutrition produce stunting and cognitive effects independent of any direct war injury.
details.energy_note: Killed slowly by the plumbing, not the ordnance.

issues.title: Sulfur mustard: the exposure that keeps arriving
issues.category_name: Chemical weapons: the exposure, and the forty years after it
issues.applies_to_note: Those with a specific exposure - a gas attack, a collapse, a siege
issues.war_form_note: Chemical and other prohibited weapons
issues.onset_note: Shows up fifteen to forty years later, or in the next generation
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Mustard gas has low mortality and very high morbidity. Its defining feature is latency: the eye, lung and skin damage that disables a survivor often appears fifteen to twenty years after an attack they thought they had survived.

details.aspect: The Iranian cohort, in numbers
details.description: Iraq used sulfur mustard against Iran in the 1980-88 war. Over 100,000 soldiers without gas masks were injured; roughly 45,000 still suffer consequences, and about 30,000 exposed Iranians have been followed as a study population.
details.energy_note: Forty years of a fortnight in 1986.
details.source_name: Balali-Mood & Darchini-Maragheh, Iran J Med Sci 2018

details.aspect: Delayed keratopathy - going blind two decades later
details.description: The eye is the most sensitive organ to sulfur mustard. Beyond the acute injury, a severe rapid-onset keratitis develops in a proportion of patients after a latent period of 15-20 years, causing permanent damage. Survivors live those twenty years knowing it may be coming.
details.energy_note: Waiting two decades to find out about your own eyes.
details.source_name: Long-term ocular complications literature; Sardasht cohort

details.aspect: 'Mustard lung' - bronchiolitis obliterans
details.description: Now considered the main pathological feature and the major cause of respiratory complication. Chronic bronchitis in 58.9% and asthma in 10.6% of one severely intoxicated cohort; imaging consistent with BO documented as late as 25 years post-exposure. Respiratory disease is the leading cause of long-term disability.
details.energy_note: Breathing as a daily, deteriorating project.

details.aspect: The psychiatric load sits on top, and was measured separately
details.description: The Sardasht-Iran Cohort Study compared 367 chemically exposed civilians against 128 from Rabat who had been exposed to intensive conventional warfare but not chemical weapons - isolating the chemical effect from general war trauma. Elevated somatisation, depression, anxiety, hostility, phobic anxiety, paranoid ideation and psychoticism.
details.energy_note: Worse than the war, and they had a control group for it.

details.aspect: Sexual dysfunction is in the clinical literature and out of the conversation
details.description: Documented alongside depression, mood disorder, anxiety and PTSD in chemical warfare survivors. It is the effect least likely to be raised by the patient and least likely to be asked about by the clinician.
details.energy_note: A documented symptom nobody in the room will name.
details.notes: Compounds the psychological material in assets/text/iran on sexual dissatisfaction and its downstream effect on work and enterprise.

details.aspect: Skin: chronic itch on old scars, and cancer risk
details.description: Persistent pruritus on decades-old lesions, multiple cherry angiomas, hypo- and hyperpigmentation, and susceptibility to skin cancers. The itch is the one that ruins sleep, permanently.
details.energy_note: Scratching a 1986 burn at three in the morning in 2026.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - the family runs a hospice for forty years
details.description: A progressively breathless, itching, sleepless, partially sighted parent is cared for at home by a spouse and children across decades. Their lives are structured around it and their own outcomes are never studied.
details.money_note: Foregone earnings of family carers over decades.
details.energy_note: A childhood spent as nursing staff.

issues.title: Halabja: gas used on a town
issues.category_name: Chemical weapons: the exposure, and the forty years after it
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Organised destruction of a group as a group
issues.onset_note: Shows up fifteen to forty years later, or in the next generation
issues.duration_note: Outlives the person it started in
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the next generation through silence, story, ritual and community
issues.summary: The largest chemical attack on a civilian-populated area in history, and the best long-run evidence available for what that does to a population and to the generations after it.

details.aspect: What happened
details.description: 16 March 1988. Between 3,200 and 5,000 killed and 7,000-10,000 injured, mostly civilians. UN investigation concluded mustard gas plus unidentified nerve agents. Part of the Anfal campaign, in which an estimated 182,000 Kurds were killed.
details.energy_note: A town, in an afternoon.

details.aspect: Thirty-eight years later, the mental health numbers
details.description: A 2026 Frontiers in Psychiatry study found PTSD in 79% of survivors, depression or anxiety in 65%, and severe somatic symptoms, with women and those of lower socioeconomic status most affected.
details.energy_note: Four fifths of a town, still, after thirty-eight years.

details.aspect: THE GENERATIONAL FINDING - and it is not genetic
details.description: A cross-generational study across three cohorts - victimised as adults, victimised as children, and not affected - found all three, including those never exposed, reported elevated depression, PTSD symptom severity and sleep disturbance. The authors note the cohorts were not genetically related, so critical life events transfer to the next generation without genetic overlap.
details.energy_note: Inherited without a gene in sight.
details.source_name: J Affect Disord, cross-generational Halabja study
details.notes: This is the single most useful row in the dataset for the question of whether transmission is genetic. Answer: partly, and it does not need to be.

details.aspect: Women's outcomes, and the neglect of them
details.description: Ovarian and cervical cancer, infertility, disabled or stillborn babies. Halabja women have publicly complained of neglect; there are few female medical specialists in or near the town to treat reproductive problems and cancers.
details.energy_note: A specific harm, and no specialist within reach of it.

details.aspect: Birth defects and cancer in the region afterwards
details.description: Preliminary surveys of the affected region showed increased rates of cancer and birth defects in the years following, alongside documented higher rates of infertility and miscarriage in exposed populations.
details.energy_note: A birth rate that carries the attack forward.

details.aspect: No services exist for the specific injury
details.description: There are no dedicated health services for sulfur mustard survivors in Iraqi Kurdistan, though registered chemical-weapons-exposed patients receive a life annuity and social benefits. Money, but no clinic.
details.money_note: Out-of-region private care for a condition with no local service.
details.energy_note: Compensated in cash for a treatment that does not exist.

details.aspect: The justice dimension does not close either
details.description: Survivors continue to seek recognition and accountability decades on. An unresolved legal status keeps the event permanently present rather than historical, which is itself a documented barrier to symptom resolution.
details.energy_note: It cannot become the past until someone says so officially.

issues.title: Living with an exposure you cannot prove
issues.category_name: Chemical weapons: the exposure, and the forty years after it
issues.applies_to_note: Those with a specific exposure - a gas attack, a collapse, a siege
issues.war_form_note: Chemical and other prohibited weapons
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Compensation, treatment and recognition all require documentation of exposure. Chemical attacks are not administered with receipts, and the people who could confirm it are frequently dead.

details.aspect: Latency destroys the causal chain in the eyes of an assessor
details.description: A lung condition appearing in 2011 from a 1987 exposure looks, to a medical board, like a lung condition. Proving the link requires records from a front-line unit in a war.
details.energy_note: Twenty-four years is long enough for nobody to believe you.

details.aspect: Civilians are documented far worse than soldiers
details.description: Military exposure produces a unit, a date and a file. Civilian exposure produces a village and a memory. Civilian survivors are systematically under-registered and therefore under-treated.
details.energy_note: Gassed off the record.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the assessment in a third country
details.description: He is 61, in Germany, with bronchiolitis obliterans and no Iranian military file. The pulmonologist has seen the pattern in the literature and writes 'consistent with'. The pension board requires 'caused by'. The two words are nine thousand euros apart.
details.energy_note: Two words, one pension.

details.aspect: Not being believed is its own injury
details.description: Survivors repeatedly describe the disbelief - medical, administrative, social - as harder than the symptoms. It converts a physical injury into a question about the person's honesty.
details.energy_note: Asked, politely, whether you are lying about being gassed.

issues.title: What healing actually looks like, chemically
issues.category_name: Chemical weapons: the exposure, and the forty years after it
issues.applies_to_note: Those with a specific exposure - a gas attack, a collapse, a siege
issues.war_form_note: Chemical and other prohibited weapons
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: There is no cure for sulfur mustard injury. Management is symptomatic, lifelong and progressive, and the honest clinical framing is slowing a decline rather than recovering from an event.

details.aspect: The treatment is a routine, not a course
details.description: Inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators, ocular lubricants and eventual surgery, emollients and antihistamines, oxygen later. Daily, indefinitely, with the dose increasing over decades.
details.money_note: Annual, lifelong.
details.energy_note: A morning routine measured in decades.

details.aspect: Research continues and the wins are marginal
details.description: Trials such as atorvastatin for inflammatory markers in mustard-induced bronchitis represent the state of the art: incremental improvement of a marker, not restoration of the lung.
details.energy_note: Progress measured in cytokines, not in breath.

details.aspect: Immune suppression means every ordinary illness is worse
details.description: Sulfur mustard suppresses immune function and bone marrow; innate immune abnormalities have been documented in Iranian veterans three decades after exposure. A winter virus is not a winter virus for these patients.
details.energy_note: Everyone else's cold is your hospital admission.

details.aspect: The psychological treatment barely exists in the same place as the physical
details.description: Pulmonology, ophthalmology, dermatology and psychiatry in four buildings, four waiting lists and four sets of notes, for one injury, in a country under sanctions.
details.energy_note: One injury, four queues, no coordination.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - the decline is visible to the family, on a schedule
details.description: Children watch a parent get measurably worse each year. The anticipatory grief starts decades before the death and does not shorten the grief afterwards.
details.energy_note: Mourning someone for twenty years while they are alive.

issues.title: Hearing, after blast
issues.category_name: The senses: hearing, sight, smell and touch after blast and gas
issues.applies_to_note: Those with a specific exposure - a gas attack, a collapse, a siege
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Tinnitus and hearing loss are among the commonest consequences of blast exposure, and a normal audiogram does not rule out a functional deficit.

details.aspect: Blast produces mixed hearing loss, not simple acoustic trauma
details.description: Both conductive and sensorineural components, which distinguishes it from occupational noise damage and means it responds differently to treatment.
details.energy_note: A different injury with the same name.

details.aspect: A clean hearing test that does not clear you
details.description: Research found objective speech-recognition performance predicted by TBI status while subjective hearing complaints were predicted by blast exposure - people with blast history have communication deficits beyond what standard audiometry predicts.
details.energy_note: Tested normal, and still cannot follow a conversation.

details.aspect: Sudden-onset tinnitus is worse than gradual
details.description: Tinnitus from blast may be more detrimental than occupational tinnitus precisely because it appears instantly rather than creeping in - there is no period of adaptation and no forewarning.
details.energy_note: A noise that starts on a Tuesday and never stops.

details.aspect: Civilians have none of the preparation
details.description: Soldiers have hearing protection, a baseline audiogram and an occupational health pathway. Civilians under bombardment have none of the three, and no record of what their hearing was before.
details.energy_note: No baseline, therefore no claim.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it takes the social life first
details.description: Restaurants, gatherings, group conversation. Withdrawal is the standard adaptation, and it is indistinguishable from depression to everyone watching.
details.energy_note: Stopped going out, and everyone assumed it was sadness.

details.aspect: It compounds every language barrier
details.description: Speech recognition in a second language is already harder. Doing it with blast-injured auditory processing in a noisy office is a compound disability that no assessment measures.
details.energy_note: Two deficits that multiply instead of adding.
details.notes: Direct interaction with the language and workplace hurdles in assets/text/iran.

issues.title: Sight, smell and the senses that carry the memory
issues.category_name: The senses: hearing, sight, smell and touch after blast and gas
issues.applies_to_note: Those with a specific exposure - a gas attack, a collapse, a siege
issues.war_form_note: Chemical and other prohibited weapons
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Vision loss after blast and gas is well documented. Smell is the one nobody treats and the one that reactivates everything.

details.aspect: Photophobia as a daily constraint
details.description: In Sardasht survivors, photophobia and ocular surface discomfort were the most significant symptoms, with bulbar conjunctival and limbal changes the predominant findings. Sunlight becomes a scheduling constraint on a life.
details.energy_note: Planning your day around the brightness of it.

details.aspect: Retinal involvement was only assessed recently
details.description: Electrophysiological assessment of 40 severely intoxicated Iranian veterans addressed the retina, which had not been examined despite well-documented anterior-segment damage - meaning survivors were assessed for decades with half the eye unexamined.
details.energy_note: Thirty years of looking at the wrong part of the eye.

details.aspect: Smell bypasses everything
details.description: Olfactory memory has direct access to limbic structures and no linguistic intermediary. Diesel, burning plastic, wet concrete, a particular disinfectant - each reproduces the state in full, in a supermarket, with no warning.
