details.energy_note: Thirty years erased by a smell in aisle four.

details.aspect: Nobody screens for it and nobody treats it
details.description: There is no standard olfactory trigger assessment in trauma care, so the most reliable reactivator of the memory is the one never addressed in the treatment plan.
details.energy_note: The main trigger, absent from every protocol.

issues.title: Blast traumatic brain injury without a visible head injury
issues.category_name: The senses: hearing, sight, smell and touch after blast and gas
issues.applies_to_note: Those with a specific exposure - a gas attack, a collapse, a siege
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Overpressure injures the brain without impact. A person with no wound, no loss of consciousness and a normal scan can have chronic post-concussive symptoms for fifteen years and more.

details.aspect: Roughly one in five blast injuries involves acute TBI
details.description: An estimated 20% of those with blast injuries suffer acute TBI, most cases mild - which is the category most likely to go unrecorded.
details.energy_note: Mild, in the sense that nobody wrote it down.

details.aspect: Symptoms persisting past fifteen years, with no direct head trauma
details.description: A documented case report describes blast-related TBI sustained with no loss of consciousness and no direct head impact, with chronic post-concussive symptoms persisting over fifteen years.
details.energy_note: Fifteen years of symptoms from an injury with no wound.

details.aspect: The symptom list is indistinguishable from a psychiatric one
details.description: Headache, tinnitus, dizziness, nausea, fatigue, hypersensitivity, irritability, memory deficits, depression. Referred to psychiatry, the neurological component goes untreated; referred to neurology, the psychological one does.
details.energy_note: Two specialties, each sure it is the other's patient.

details.aspect: The mechanism is degenerative, not static
details.description: Animal work indicates blast TBI produces auditory neurodegeneration, chronic vascular remodelling and blood-brain barrier degradation, associated with increased post-blast stroke and haemorrhage risk.
details.energy_note: An injury that continues working after the war.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the man who is not lazy
details.description: He was thrown against a wall by pressure in 2014 and walked away. In 2026 he cannot hold a schedule, loses words mid-sentence and sleeps eleven hours. Three employers have concluded he does not want to work.
details.energy_note: Fired repeatedly for a brain injury nobody recorded.

issues.title: Amputation and the life built around it
issues.category_name: Permanent disability, physical and psychiatric
issues.applies_to_note: Those left with a permanent impairment
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: A prosthesis is not a solution, it is a subscription. Sockets need refitting, components wear out, children outgrow limbs every year, and all of it must be paid for in a country whose supply chain is under sanction.

details.aspect: A child's prosthesis is replaced roughly annually
details.description: Growth means refitting or replacement every 12 to 18 months through childhood, each one a cost, a fitting, a period of adjustment and a school absence.
details.money_note: Per replacement, recurring.
details.energy_note: A new leg every school year.

details.aspect: Sanctions reach the socket
details.description: Components, resins and fitting equipment are imported. Restrictions on banking, shipping and insurance that block medicine block prosthetics the same way, and there is no humanitarian-exemption argument for a pylon.
details.energy_note: A leg held up by a letter of credit.

details.aspect: Phantom limb pain, which is neurological and is treated as complaining
details.description: Real, frequently severe, poorly responsive to ordinary analgesia, and routinely dismissed because the limb in question is not there.
details.energy_note: Agony in a leg you can see is gone.

details.aspect: Identity reorganisation is the psychological work, and it is not brief
details.description: The task is not accepting a lost limb but rebuilding who the person is - worker, parent, partner, body. It takes years and there is usually no psychological support attached to the surgical pathway at all.
details.energy_note: Surgery in a week, a self in five years.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - the household reorganises permanently around it
details.description: One injury converts a spouse into a carer, a child into an assistant, and a two-income household into a none-income household. The measured cost of the injury is the surgery.
details.energy_note: One limb, four lives rewritten.

issues.title: Psychiatric disability, and the fact that it is a disability
issues.category_name: Permanent disability, physical and psychiatric
issues.applies_to_note: Those left with a permanent impairment
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Severe, chronic war-related psychiatric illness is disabling in exactly the way a physical injury is, and is treated by almost every system - medical, legal, familial - as something the person could stop doing.

details.aspect: It removes capacity for work as reliably as an amputation
details.description: Concentration, tolerance of unpredictability, interpersonal capacity and sleep are all requirements of employment, and war-related illness takes all four at once.
details.money_note: Lifetime foregone earnings.
details.energy_note: Unemployable, and told it is an attitude problem.

details.aspect: Disability systems are built for visible injuries
details.description: Assessment forms ask about stairs, lifting and distance walked. A person unable to leave the house because of hypervigilance scores well on all of them and is found fit.
details.money_note: Benefits denied on an inapplicable assessment.
details.energy_note: Passing a test that measures the wrong thing.

details.aspect: Stigma is heavier where the war came from
details.description: In many of the societies producing these injuries, psychiatric illness is a family reputational matter. Treatment is avoided, concealed, or sought in another city under another name.
details.money_note: Private care chosen to avoid a record.
details.energy_note: Paying extra so no one finds out.

details.aspect: Medication access is a sanctions problem too
details.description: Antipsychotics, mood stabilisers and modern antidepressants are imported or made from imported ingredients. In shortage, substitution and interruption are the norm, and both destabilise a stabilised patient.
details.energy_note: Stable for two years, then the supply changes.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the brother who is 'not well'
details.description: He has lived in the back room since 2009. The family says he is not well. He has never been assessed, never been treated, never claimed anything, and appears in no statistic about the war he was in.
details.energy_note: A whole life, unrecorded, in a back room.

issues.title: Being disabled in a country that was damaged too
issues.category_name: Permanent disability, physical and psychiatric
issues.applies_to_note: Those left with a permanent impairment
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.summary: Disability is produced by the interaction of an impairment with an environment. War damages the environment at the same time as it produces the impairment, so the same injury is far more disabling than it would be elsewhere.

details.aspect: Lifts do not run without power
details.description: A wheelchair user on the fifth floor of a building with intermittent electricity is housebound on an unpredictable schedule set by the grid.
details.energy_note: Your front door opens when the power says so.

details.aspect: Rehabilitation services are the first to close and the last to reopen
details.description: Physiotherapy, occupational therapy and prosthetics are classified as non-urgent during a conflict and are not restored quickly afterwards, which is precisely when the recoverable window for function closes.
details.energy_note: The therapy arrives after it would have worked.

details.aspect: Rubble is a mobility barrier for a decade
details.description: Cleared roads are not accessible roads. Broken pavements, missing kerb cuts and rebuilt buildings without lifts persist long after reconstruction is declared complete.
details.energy_note: A city rebuilt, and still not walkable to you.

issues.title: There is no mental health system left
issues.category_name: Treatment: what healing actually costs, and how far it goes
issues.applies_to_note: Anyone physically present in a war zone
issues.war_form_note: Bombs, missiles, artillery, invasion, ground fighting
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: The collapse of services is simultaneous with the surge in need. The population most requiring psychiatric care is in the place where psychiatric care has just been destroyed.

details.aspect: Documented directly in the current Gaza reviews
details.description: A 2024-25 review reports 70-90% of children in Gaza meeting criteria for PTSD or showing significant depression and anxiety symptoms, explicitly 'exacerbated by the collapse of mental health services'.
details.energy_note: Maximum need, zero supply, same postcode.

details.aspect: Clinicians are in the same war
details.description: Therapists treating continuous traumatic stress are themselves living under it - a dynamic the recent literature addresses explicitly as therapists working on a shared axis of exposure rather than outside it.
details.energy_note: Your therapist heard the same explosion.

details.aspect: What scales is school-based and cheap
details.description: The programmes with evidence behind them are group, school-based and delivered by trained teachers, not individual therapy by scarce clinicians. This is the actionable finding in the entire treatment literature.
details.money_note: Per child, group delivery.
details.energy_note: It works, it is cheap, and it is rarely funded.

details.aspect: Untreated for a decade is a different illness
details.description: Early intervention changes trajectory. A decade of untreated PTSD produces entrenched avoidance, secondary depression, substance use and relationship loss that then all need treating in their own right.
details.energy_note: Four diagnoses where there was one.

issues.title: Being treated abroad, by people with no reference for it
issues.category_name: Treatment: what healing actually costs, and how far it goes
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Resettled survivors reach functioning health systems and encounter clinicians with no framework for the event, no shared language and a fifty-minute appointment.

details.aspect: Interpretation changes what can be said
details.description: Trauma disclosure through a third person, often from the same community, frequently stops the disclosure entirely - particularly for sexual violence, collaboration, and anything the community would judge.
details.energy_note: A translator from your own city, in the room.

details.aspect: Waiting lists outlast the crisis
details.description: Specialist trauma services in most destination countries run six to eighteen month waits. The person presents at the point of crisis and is offered an appointment after the crisis has resolved itself one way or another.
details.energy_note: Booked in for after it stops mattering.

details.aspect: The wrong treatment first, as standard
details.description: Six sessions of CBT for what is moral injury, or an SSRI for what is continuous traumatic stress about family still under threat. Not negligence - just the default pathway, applied to a case it was not designed for.
details.energy_note: Correct procedure, wrong problem.

details.aspect: Disclosure has immigration consequences
details.description: A psychiatric record can affect visa, asylum credibility, custody and citizenship in ways that vary by country and are rarely explained. Many people rationally decline treatment for this reason.
details.energy_note: Getting help, at the possible price of status.
details.notes: Interacts directly with the status and discretion issues in assets/text/iran.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - one bad experience ends help-seeking permanently
details.description: A dismissive first appointment produces a person who will not try again for fifteen years, and who tells their community not to bother either.
details.energy_note: One bad hour, a decade of nobody going.

issues.title: What recovery actually means, and what it does not
issues.category_name: Treatment: what healing actually costs, and how far it goes
issues.applies_to_note: Anyone physically present in a war zone
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Some of this resolves. Some of it becomes manageable. Some of it is permanent. Treating all three as the same category is how both patients and clinicians end up feeling they have failed.

details.aspect: Symptoms fall away fast when the threat genuinely ends
details.description: The continuous-traumatic-stress evidence is direct: once a resident leaves the affected area, symptoms subside dramatically. Safety, where it is real, is itself the most effective single intervention.
details.energy_note: The treatment is often a different postcode.

details.aspect: Nightmare-focused work has the best ratio of cost to effect
details.description: In the Better Learning Programme cohort, roughly half reported no nightmares after treatment and a further 47% reduced frequency - from a school-delivered intervention.
details.energy_note: Half of them simply stopped having them.

details.aspect: Permanent things stay permanent
details.description: Bronchiolitis obliterans does not reverse. A retina does not regrow. Delayed keratopathy at 20 years is not preventable by therapy. Honest framing here protects the patient from believing they failed at recovering.
details.energy_note: Naming what will not get better is also care.

details.aspect: Post-traumatic growth is real and is not the point
details.description: Some survivors do report deepened relationships and changed priorities. Presenting that as the expected outcome converts it into another standard the person is failing to meet.
details.energy_note: Don't make them grow on schedule.

issues.title: Being attacked as a category rather than an individual
issues.category_name: Genocide and mass atrocity: what it destroys beyond the dead
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Organised destruction of a group as a group
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Outlives the person it started in
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the next generation through silence, story, ritual and community
issues.summary: Ordinary war damage is impersonal - you were in the wrong place. Genocidal violence is the opposite: it is precisely about who you are, and that changes what the survivor concludes about themselves.

details.aspect: The identity becomes the injury
details.description: There is no behaviour that would have avoided it, because the target was a characteristic. That removes the illusion of control that ordinary trauma survivors use to function.
details.energy_note: Nothing you could have done differently, ever.

details.aspect: Children inherit the category with the name
details.description: A child born afterwards carries the same identifier that was the criterion for the attack. They did not experience the event and they hold the category that produced it.
details.energy_note: Born already on the list.

details.aspect: Denial keeps it open indefinitely
details.description: Where the event is officially disputed, survivors spend decades arguing about whether it happened instead of recovering from it. Recognition is not a symbolic matter; it is a clinical variable.
details.energy_note: Litigating your own memory for forty years.

details.aspect: Language, ritual and trade go with the people
details.description: What is destroyed is not only lives but the transmission mechanism of a culture - the people who knew the songs, the recipes, the dialect and the craft. The loss continues after the killing stops.
details.energy_note: A culture with its teachers removed.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - identity becomes either armour or a thing to hide
details.description: Descendants split into those for whom it is the organising fact of life and those who conceal it entirely. Both are responses to the same event and they frequently cannot talk to each other.
details.energy_note: Two kinds of grandchild, in the same family.

issues.title: Sexual violence as a weapon, and the silence around it
issues.category_name: Genocide and mass atrocity: what it destroys beyond the dead
issues.applies_to_note: Where the effect lands specifically or disproportionately on women
issues.war_form_note: Organised destruction of a group as a group
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Outlives the person it started in
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the next generation through silence, story, ritual and community
issues.summary: Mass sexual violence is a standard instrument of genocidal and ethnic campaigns, and it is the one category of war injury that the victim's own community most reliably punishes them for.

details.aspect: The injury is compounded by the response to it
details.description: Rejection by spouse or family, unmarriageability, removal from the household. The social consequence is frequently more destructive than the assault, and is entirely a decision made by the victim's own people.
details.energy_note: Attacked twice, the second time at home.

details.aspect: Disclosure is rationally avoided
details.description: Since the consequence of telling is often exile from the family, non-disclosure is a correct strategy. Which means prevalence is systematically understated in every dataset, including this one.
details.energy_note: A number nobody has, on purpose.

details.aspect: Children born of it occupy an impossible position
details.description: Identified with the attacker, raised by the attacked, belonging to neither, and often without legal status or documented parentage.
details.energy_note: A child who is evidence.

details.aspect: Men are victims too, and are documented almost nowhere
details.description: Sexual violence against men in detention is a recognised and systematically under-reported instrument. Disclosure rates are lower still, and services essentially do not exist.
details.energy_note: A category of victim with no services at all.
details.notes: Deliberately included: the male-specific material in assets/text/iran does not cover this and it belongs somewhere.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it removes the family as a support structure
details.description: The single most protective factor after war trauma is family support. This injury specifically destroys it, which is why the outcomes are so much worse.
details.energy_note: The one injury that takes the cure with it.

issues.title: Erasure: when the place stops being yours
issues.category_name: Genocide and mass atrocity: what it destroys beyond the dead
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Organised destruction of a group as a group
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Outlives the person it started in
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the next generation through silence, story, ritual and community
issues.summary: Renamed streets, demolished cemeteries, rewritten curricula, a new population in the same houses. The survivor's memory becomes officially incorrect.

details.aspect: Return becomes impossible in a sense that has nothing to do with travel
details.description: The address exists, the building exists, and nothing that made it home does. Physical return delivers the loss again rather than resolving it.
details.energy_note: You can go back. There is nothing there to go back to.

details.aspect: Graves are the specific wound
details.description: Destroyed or inaccessible cemeteries remove the one physical site where grief is conventionally performed, and there is no substitute for it.
details.energy_note: Nowhere to put the flowers.

details.aspect: The archive war
details.description: Land registries, birth records and parish books destroyed or altered means descendants cannot document ancestry, claim property, or prove they are from where they are from.
details.energy_note: Your grandfather, unprovable.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the street on the map application
details.description: He types the name he grew up with. It offers him a correction. He accepts the correction, because he wants to see the satellite image, and something in that transaction stays with him for the rest of the week.
details.energy_note: Autocorrected out of your own childhood.

issues.title: A war with no explosion and the same casualties
issues.category_name: Sanctions: war conducted through the economy
issues.applies_to_note: A civilian population under economic war, whether or not shots are fired
issues.war_form_note: Sanctions, snapback, de-risking, financial exclusion
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Comprehensive sanctions are an instrument of war aimed at a civilian population. They produce mortality, disability and psychiatric illness through the health system, the supply chain and the currency instead of through ordnance.

details.aspect: The scale of the shortage, stated by the regulator's own side
details.description: About 800 pharmaceutical products in short supply nationwide, including 90 classed as essential and life-saving, per the Iranian Pharmacists Association spokesman.
details.energy_note: Ninety life-saving drugs, absent, at once.

details.aspect: The humanitarian exemption does not function
details.description: Medicine is formally exempt. Restrictions on banking, shipping and insurance mean importers cannot pay for or transport it, so the exemption exists on paper while the shelf is empty.
details.energy_note: Legally permitted, practically impossible.
details.source_name: Peer-reviewed: health service disruption under sanctions

details.aspect: It reaches the patient as delay, substitution and death
details.description: A qualitative study of Iranian cancer care found sanctions restricted access to standard equipment and modern technology, producing delays, misdiagnosis and diagnostic and therapeutic side effects 'to the point of death'. Some patients discontinued treatment entirely.
details.energy_note: Dying of a banking regulation.

details.aspect: Currency allocation is the real rationing mechanism
details.description: After the UN snapback, about USD 3.4bn was allocated for medicines and equipment, and hard-currency availability had already cut effective access to that funding by 10 to 20 percent. The rationing is done by exchange rate, invisibly.
details.money_note: Patient-side cost of drugs bought at unofficial rates.
details.energy_note: Rationed by a number on a screen in another country.

details.aspect: The psychological effect is specific: it is being slowly told you do not count
details.description: Unlike a strike, sanctions produce no single moment and no image. The message received over years is that the suffering of the population is an acceptable instrument, which corrodes something different from fear.
details.energy_note: Not terror. A long, formal insult.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the MS patient and the three pharmacies
details.description: Her interferon has been unavailable for five weeks. The pharmacist suggests a domestic substitute he cannot vouch for, at four times last year's price, in a currency that lost a third of its value since her last prescription. She takes it, because the alternative is nothing.
details.energy_note: Injecting something you hope is the same drug.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it makes the population blame itself
details.description: Shortage is experienced as domestic failure - corruption, incompetence, hoarding - which is also partly true. The result is a population angry at itself about a condition imposed from outside, which is politically useful to everyone except the population.
details.energy_note: Furious at the wrong people, correctly.

details.aspect: How this dataset relates to the other two
details.description: assets/text/general lists what is imposed on anyone. assets/text/iran lists what is imposed on top by nationality and status. This file lists what is imposed on top of that by war, in whatever form it is being conducted. They are additive: an Iranian under sanctions queues for medicine (here), proves identity to a visa officer (iran), and waits on hold to a call centre that cannot help (general), in the same week.
details.energy_note: Three stacked queues, in the same week, for one person.
details.notes: Read the three listissue.csv files side by side; the schemas are aligned.

issues.title: Domestic production struck as well
issues.category_name: Sanctions: war conducted through the economy
issues.applies_to_note: A civilian population under economic war, whether or not shots are fired
issues.war_form_note: Sanctions, snapback, de-risking, financial exclusion
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Where sanctions are combined with kinetic strikes on pharmaceutical and medical manufacturing, the substitution route that made the sanctions survivable is removed at the same time.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the manufacturer's own account
details.description: A company sales director told Al Jazeera that Israeli strikes hit all of its research and production lines, including peptide and narcotic active ingredients and anticancer drugs, noting the customer base was predominantly cancer and chronic disease patients.
details.energy_note: The factory that made the workaround, bombed.

details.aspect: Quality falls before supply does
details.description: Historic sanctions waves forced imports of raw materials of lower or questionable quality and disrupted generic production. Patients experience this as a drug that no longer works, and are told it is the same drug.
details.energy_note: The tablet is the same and your symptoms are back.

details.aspect: Trust in medicine itself erodes
details.description: After repeated substitutions and counterfeits, patients stop believing the pharmacy, which produces non-adherence, self-medication and reliance on informal supply that is genuinely dangerous.
details.energy_note: Stopped trusting the one system you needed.

issues.title: Sanctions as a planning-horizon weapon
issues.category_name: Sanctions: war conducted through the economy
issues.applies_to_note: A civilian population under economic war, whether or not shots are fired
issues.war_form_note: Sanctions, snapback, de-risking, financial exclusion
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: The most durable psychological effect of long-running economic war is the removal of the future as a usable concept. Nobody can plan five years ahead, so nobody does, and the behaviour that produces is then blamed on the culture.

details.aspect: Savings are not a rational act under 40% inflation
details.description: Holding the currency is a guaranteed loss, so households convert to goods, gold or dollars, or spend. The resulting absence of savings is then read abroad as financial illiteracy.
details.money_note: Real value of savings destroyed.
details.energy_note: Punished for not saving in a currency that eats itself.

details.aspect: Long-horizon decisions stop being made
details.description: Training for a profession, starting a company, having a child, buying a house. All require an assumption of continuity, and the assumption is not available.
details.energy_note: A life lived in three-month increments.

details.aspect: Emigration becomes the only plan anyone has
details.description: When the domestic future is unusable, the entire national conversation reduces to leaving. That is itself a psychological condition affecting people who never go.
details.energy_note: A country where the only plan is the exit.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it hollows out the professional class first
details.description: Doctors, engineers and academics have the mobility to act on it, so they do. The health system loses the staff at the same time it loses the drugs.
details.energy_note: The people who could fix it leaving because of it.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the deferred wedding
details.description: They were going to marry in 2023 and buy a flat. Then the rial moved again. They are still engaged, still in their parents' houses, aged 33 and 31, and they no longer discuss the date.
details.energy_note: Engaged indefinitely, by exchange rate.

issues.title: Mental health care under economic war
issues.category_name: Sanctions: war conducted through the economy
issues.applies_to_note: A civilian population under economic war, whether or not shots are fired
issues.war_form_note: Sanctions, snapback, de-risking, financial exclusion
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Psychiatric medicine is import-dependent, psychotherapy is unaffordable at a collapsed exchange rate, and the population needing both is the one the sanctions and the war are being applied to.

details.aspect: Interruption destabilises stable patients
details.description: Lithium, clozapine, depot antipsychotics and modern antidepressants do not tolerate gaps. A supply interruption produces relapse, hospitalisation and sometimes a permanent step down in baseline function.
details.energy_note: Two good years undone by a shipping problem.

details.aspect: Therapy priced in a collapsing currency
details.description: A session that cost a manageable fraction of a monthly wage in 2017 costs a large one now. Treatment becomes a luxury good in the middle of a mental health emergency.
details.money_note: Per session, against a collapsed wage.
details.energy_note: Priced out of your own recovery.

details.aspect: Research and training are cut off too
details.description: Sanctions restrict conference attendance, journal access, software and equipment, so the clinical workforce falls behind - a slow degradation of care quality that nobody experiences as an event.
details.energy_note: A profession quietly falling behind the field.

issues.title: Hunger as a psychological instrument
issues.category_name: Siege, blockade and hunger
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Encirclement, blockade, deliberate deprivation
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Deliberate deprivation does specific and well-characterised things to cognition and behaviour, and those effects are then presented as evidence about the character of the besieged population.

details.aspect: Starvation narrows cognition to food
details.description: Sustained caloric restriction produces obsessive preoccupation with food, irritability, apathy, social withdrawal and loss of libido - documented since the Minnesota Starvation Experiment and reproduced in every siege since.
details.energy_note: A mind with one subject left in it.

details.aspect: Feeding a child you cannot feed
details.description: The specific injury to a parent is not their own hunger. It is dividing insufficient food in front of children and deciding, daily, who gets less.
details.energy_note: Arithmetic, performed on your own children.

details.aspect: Queueing for food under fire
details.description: Aid distribution concentrates people in a known location at a known time, which is a recognised and recurring danger. The choice is between hunger and a crowd.
details.energy_note: Standing in the open because the alternative is hunger.

details.aspect: The prenatal cohort is created here
details.description: Maternal malnutrition during a siege produces the exposure documented in the famine-epigenetics literature - see NEU-002. The measurable outcome arrives in fifty years.
details.energy_note: A siege with a fifty-year receipt.

issues.title: Water, sewage, and the dignity floor
issues.category_name: Siege, blockade and hunger
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Encirclement, blockade, deliberate deprivation
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: The psychological literature on siege focuses on food. Survivors more often describe sanitation - the specific humiliation of having nowhere clean to wash, defecate or menstruate.

details.aspect: Shame is the reported emotion, not fear
details.description: Adults describe the loss of privacy and cleanliness as the part that destroyed their sense of themselves as adults. It is rarely asked about and reliably volunteered.
details.energy_note: Not frightened. Ashamed.

details.aspect: Menstruation under siege
details.description: No products, no privacy, no water, no disposal, in a mixed shelter. Women and girls report deliberately restricting food and fluid to reduce the problem.
details.energy_note: Eating less, so that you bleed less.

details.aspect: Children's illness cycles compound the developmental effect
details.description: Repeated diarrhoeal disease in early childhood produces stunting and cognitive effects that outlast the siege by a lifetime.
details.energy_note: A permanent effect from temporary plumbing.

details.aspect: It is the detail people cannot say afterwards
details.description: Survivors will describe shelling in detail and will not describe this, which means it is absent from most accounts and most assessments.
details.energy_note: The part that never makes it into the testimony.

issues.title: The passport as a wall
issues.category_name: Immobility: the passport, the visa, the country you cannot leave or re-enter
issues.applies_to_note: A civilian population under economic war, whether or not shots are fired
issues.war_form_note: Passports, visas, closed airspace, bans on movement
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: A travel document that no one will accept converts the entire world outside the border into a theoretical place. That is a psychological condition, not an administrative one.

details.aspect: Where the Iranian passport sits, 2026
details.description: Henley: visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 40 countries, ranked 90th. Other indices: 95th with 45 destinations, 86th with a mobility score of 51, and 190th of 199 on one measure. No visa-free access to the Schengen area at all.
details.energy_note: Forty countries. The rest require permission you will not get.

details.aspect: Refusal rates, and what applying costs
details.description: US State Department data for FY2024 gave an adjusted B-1/B-2 refusal rate of 55.54% for Iranian nationals. Each attempt costs a fee, a journey to a third country to find an embassy, hotels, and time off work - all non-refundable on refusal.
details.money_note: Per attempt, including third-country travel.
details.energy_note: A coin flip you pay four figures to call.

details.aspect: The 2026 ban is categorical
details.description: Proclamation 10998 bans issuance of all immigrant and nonimmigrant visa categories for Iranian nationals from 1 January 2026, with no expiry and 180-day reviews. F-1 students are included this time, unlike 2017. USCIS has placed an indefinite adjudication hold on virtually all pending benefits for Iranian nationals.
details.energy_note: Not a hard queue. A closed door with no number on it.

details.aspect: Barred outright from entry to specific states
details.description: Iranian passport holders are barred from entering Libya, Syria, the UAE and the United States - the UAE being the regional hub that most Iranian business and family travel routes through.
details.energy_note: The hub your whole region routes through, closed.

details.aspect: Airspace closure removes even the countries that would have you
details.description: In January 2026 Iran issued a NOTAM closing airspace to all flights without prior permission; flight tracking showed aircraft denied entry or rerouted. The 2026 war closed airspace across multiple countries and stranded hundreds of thousands.
details.energy_note: The forty countries are also unreachable this week.

details.aspect: The psychological shape of it: a life with a ceiling
details.description: Conferences not attended, jobs not applied for, a sibling's wedding not reached, a parent's funeral missed. The effect is not a single blocked trip but a lifetime of pre-emptive self-exclusion from anything requiring a border.
details.energy_note: Not applying, because why would you.

issues.title: Not being able to go back either
issues.category_name: Immobility: the passport, the visa, the country you cannot leave or re-enter
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: Passports, visas, closed airspace, bans on movement
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Immobility is symmetrical and the second direction is discussed far less. For many, returning means conscription, an open case, an exit ban, or simply not being certain of getting out again.

details.aspect: The unrepeatable visit
details.description: Going back may be a one-way action. So the visit to a dying parent is weighed against a residence permit, a career and a marriage, and the person decides not to go, and then lives with having decided that.
details.energy_note: Choosing your life over your mother's last week.

details.aspect: Military service as a permanent tether
details.description: An unresolved conscription obligation makes return an arrest. It attaches specifically to men and does not expire on any schedule the person controls.
details.energy_note: A border you are legally free to cross once.

details.aspect: Being unable to return corrodes the identity claim
details.description: Over years, a person who cannot go back stops being able to speak about the place in the present tense. They become an expert on a country that no longer exists in the form they knew.
details.energy_note: A citizen of a place that has moved on without you.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it distorts every political opinion
details.description: Those who cannot return hold positions with no personal cost attached; those inside pay for every position. The resulting mutual contempt splits diaspora communities permanently.
details.energy_note: Opinions from people who will never pay for them.

issues.title: Statelessness in practice, if not in law
issues.category_name: Immobility: the passport, the visa, the country you cannot leave or re-enter
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: Passports, visas, closed airspace, bans on movement
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Someone whose passport cannot be renewed abroad, whose country's consulate is closed, and whose host country will not regularise them, has all the properties of statelessness without the legal status that comes with protections.

details.aspect: The consulate closes and the document expires anyway
details.description: Severed relations mean no renewal. The document runs out on schedule regardless, and on that date the person's legal existence abroad begins to unwind.
details.energy_note: A countdown you cannot stop or appeal.

details.aspect: Renewing requires dealing with the state you fled
details.description: For a political refugee this is a direct contradiction: legal existence abroad requires approaching the authority the asylum claim is based on fearing.
details.energy_note: Ask the people you fled for permission to exist.

details.aspect: Everything downstream fails at once
details.description: Work permit, driving licence, bank account, tenancy, health cover and marriage registration all key off the document. One expiry cascades through an entire life within months.
details.energy_note: One expiry date, nine collapses.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the expired passport in Tbilisi
details.description: It ran out in March. The consulate is not issuing. His lease renewal needs a valid document, his employer's payroll system has flagged it, and the bank has restricted the account. He has not committed any act; a date passed.
details.energy_note: Illegal by the calendar.

issues.title: The account closed in a country you are not at war with
issues.category_name: Financial exclusion abroad: being a nationality a bank cannot afford
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: Sanctions, snapback, de-risking, financial exclusion
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: De-risking means a bank in a third country closes an ordinary person's account because of where they were born. It is not a sanction, it is a bank deciding the person is not worth the compliance cost.

details.aspect: Armenia - the criterion was place of birth
details.description: Iranian citizens found accounts frozen, with banks across the country applying policies affecting all clients listing Iran as place of birth, regardless of ethnicity or current citizenship.
details.energy_note: Closed for a line on a birth certificate.

details.aspect: Georgia - the visa-free country that stopped banking you
details.description: Georgia waived visas for Iranians from 2011 and became one of the few accessible destinations. The Iran-Georgia Chamber of Commerce reported accounts closed and banks tightening account-opening rules for Iranian citizens.
details.energy_note: Welcome to enter. Not to hold money.

details.aspect: UAE - banks acting on their own initiative
details.description: Emirati banks blocked the accounts of roughly 400 Iranian companies over a period of weeks and refused to open accounts even for dual nationals. Reporting notes these limits were not officially mandated by the governments - the lenders initiated them.
details.energy_note: Nobody ordered it. It happened anyway.

details.aspect: It reaches citizens of the destination country too
details.description: A 2024 FinCEN comment from the National Iranian American Council documented Bank of America identifying as many as 15,000 accounts connected to people of Iranian heritage that had been restricted, and described the problem as systemic across the sector, including Wells Fargo de-risking affecting hundreds of customers.
details.energy_note: A US citizen, de-banked for a grandparent.

details.aspect: There is no appeal, because there is no accusation
details.description: A closure letter gives no reason, because giving one may constitute tipping off. The customer cannot rebut a case that was never stated, and every subsequent bank sees a closed account.
details.energy_note: Convicted with no charge, no court, and a permanent record.

details.aspect: The psychological content is specific: it is being treated as contaminated
details.description: Not accused of anything, not charged, simply not worth the risk. People describe it as being told they are a hazardous material rather than a person.
details.energy_note: Not guilty. Just not worth the paperwork.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the salary that will not land
details.description: He teaches at a university in Yerevan. In week three the bank calls, politely, to say the account is being closed under policy. His employer cannot pay him in cash. His landlord takes bank transfer only.
details.energy_note: Employed, housed, and financially unreachable.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it teaches the whole family to expect exclusion
details.description: Children watch a parent be refused, repeatedly, for nothing. The lesson learned is that institutions are not for them, and that lesson persists into a generation with different passports.
details.energy_note: Raised to expect the no.

issues.title: Squeezed from both sides at once
issues.category_name: Financial exclusion abroad: being a nationality a bank cannot afford
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: Sanctions, snapback, de-risking, financial exclusion
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Foreign banks close the account for being Iranian, and the Iranian state freezes assets of citizens abroad it disapproves of. The person is excluded by both jurisdictions simultaneously.

details.aspect: The home state does it too
details.description: Iran has moved to seize assets of more than 100 citizens abroad and freeze their bank accounts. Exclusion is not the monopoly of the sanctioning side.
details.energy_note: Locked out of both countries' banking at once.

details.aspect: Inheritance becomes untouchable
details.description: A flat in Tehran left to a child in Toronto cannot be sold, the proceeds cannot be transferred, and declaring the asset abroad may create tax liability on money that can never be received.
details.energy_note: Taxed on money you will never see.

details.aspect: Sending money home is a criminal-adjacent act
details.description: Supporting parents requires informal transfer networks. The sender is exposed to prosecution in the host country and the recipient to attention at home, for the act of giving a pension to a mother.
details.money_note: Transfer premium, per remittance.
details.energy_note: Breaking a law to send your mother her rent.

details.aspect: Operation Economic Outcast raised the stakes again
details.description: Announced 24 August 2026, expanding sanctions risk for anyone doing business with Iran, with Treasury warning that facilitating entities will be cut off from the US financial system. Every bank in the world reads that as a reason to close more accounts.
details.energy_note: Each announcement closes another thousand accounts.

issues.title: Paying more for everything, permanently
issues.category_name: Financial exclusion abroad: being a nationality a bank cannot afford
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: Sanctions, snapback, de-risking, financial exclusion
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Financial exclusion is not binary. Most people are not cut off; they are surcharged - worse rates, more checks, more documents, more delays, forever.

details.aspect: The friction tax
details.description: Every transfer reviewed, every large payment queried, every new account a three-week process with extra documents. Individually minor, cumulatively a permanent surcharge on an ordinary financial life.
details.money_note: Annual, in fees, spreads and lost opportunity.
details.energy_note: A percentage taken off the top of your whole life.

details.aspect: Credit builds slower or not at all
details.description: Restricted products, refused cards, higher rates. Ten years later the mortgage is more expensive or unavailable, which is a six-figure difference produced by a nationality.
details.energy_note: A worse mortgage for a worse birthplace.

details.aspect: Business becomes impossible at the payments layer
details.description: A consultant cannot invoice, a shop cannot take card payments, a startup cannot get a merchant account. The entrepreneurship the host country says it wants is blocked at the plumbing.
details.energy_note: Allowed to work, not allowed to be paid.

issues.title: Watching money disappear while you hold it
issues.category_name: The economy inside your head: inflation, savings, planning horizon
issues.applies_to_note: A civilian population under economic war, whether or not shots are fired
issues.war_form_note: Sanctions, snapback, de-risking, financial exclusion
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Hyperinflation is experienced as a continuous small theft. The psychological effect is distinct from poverty: it is the loss of the relationship between effort and reward.

details.aspect: Work stops producing a predictable result
details.description: A salary negotiated in spring is worth substantially less by autumn without anything happening. Effort and outcome decouple, which is the precondition for learned helplessness.
details.energy_note: Working harder and having less, reliably.

details.aspect: Constant mental arithmetic in two currencies
details.description: Every purchase is converted, compared to last month, and weighed against whether to buy now or after the next move. It is a permanent background computation running on everybody.
details.energy_note: A calculator that never switches off.

details.aspect: A generation's savings erased more than once
details.description: Those who lived through several devaluations have had the same lesson delivered repeatedly: accumulation does not work here. That belief does not reverse when they emigrate.
details.energy_note: Taught three times that saving is for fools.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it follows them abroad as financial behaviour
details.description: Reluctance to use banks, preference for cash, gold and property, distrust of pensions and insurance. All rational where they learned it, all costly where they now live.
details.energy_note: Correct instincts, wrong country.

issues.title: The cost of the war is billed to the household
issues.category_name: The economy inside your head: inflation, savings, planning horizon
issues.applies_to_note: Non-combatant civilians specifically
issues.war_form_note: Sanctions, snapback, de-risking, financial exclusion
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Reconstruction, defence and sanctions absorption are all ultimately paid out of household consumption, usually through inflation and subsidy removal rather than through anything a citizen can see or vote on.

details.aspect: Rebuilding what you already paid for once
details.description: The same family pays for the house, then for the repair, then in taxes for the national reconstruction, and receives a rebuilt building that is worth less than the one that stood there.
details.energy_note: Buying your own house three times.

details.aspect: Insurance does not cover acts of war
details.description: War exclusion clauses are standard. Every private policy a household holds becomes void for exactly the event that occurred.
details.energy_note: Insured against everything except this.

details.aspect: The compensation scheme, if there is one, arrives years late and partial
details.description: Registration windows, documentary requirements and valuations at pre-war prices in post-war currency mean that most claimants receive a fraction, several years after they needed it.
details.energy_note: Paid a quarter of it, four years later.

issues.title: The recognised clinical burden of watching from outside
issues.category_name: Diaspora: watching it from outside
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: Blackouts, jamming, propaganda, disinformation
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the next generation through silence, story, ritual and community
issues.summary: Distance is protective against blast and not against much else. The diaspora symptom profile is now described in the medical literature as a distinct and under-recognised burden.

details.aspect: The symptom list, as published
details.description: Sleep disturbance, somatic complaints, worsening of pre-existing depression or anxiety, moral distress and survivor guilt, and impaired functioning linked to compulsive news consumption and nocturnal monitoring of events.
details.energy_note: A diagnosis for people who were never there.

details.aspect: It stacks on the previous ones
details.description: For Iranians abroad the 2026 conflict intersects with earlier upheavals in Iran, amplifying transnational stressors through identity and kinship ties. This is not a first trauma; it is the fourth or fifth, in the same nervous system.
details.energy_note: Not a new wound. The same one, reopened.

details.aspect: Work performance falls and nobody attributes it correctly
details.description: The employee is up at 03:00 checking whether a district was struck, and at 09:00 in a meeting about quarterly targets. Performance management follows in due course.
details.energy_note: Disciplined for a war on another continent.

details.aspect: Collective action is the identified protective factor
details.description: The literature identifies diaspora mobilisation - large-scale demonstrations, organised solidarity - as what converts helplessness into agency, and communication blackouts and internal political fracture as what prevents it.
details.energy_note: The thing that helps is a crowd.

details.aspect: The 5-4-3-2-1 advice, and its limits
details.description: Clinicians recommend sensory grounding. It works for an acute spike and it does not address the actual problem, which is that the person's mother is in a city being bombed.
details.energy_note: Grounding techniques for an ungrounded situation.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the 3am pattern
details.description: Tehran is three and a half hours ahead of London. The strikes are at night there, which is early evening here, and the news arrives as he is putting his daughter to bed. He has done this for six weeks. She has started asking why he checks his phone during the story.
details.energy_note: A child learning the time difference.

issues.title: Being asked to explain your country at work
issues.category_name: Diaspora: watching it from outside
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: During a war, every colleague, acquaintance and stranger with an opinion treats the nearest person of that nationality as a spokesman, an explanation service, or a proxy defendant.

details.aspect: The question is never neutral
details.description: 'So what do you think about what's happening?' asked in a kitchen, by someone with a position already formed, of a person whose cousin is not answering their phone.
details.energy_note: A geopolitical debate while you are waiting for a text.

details.aspect: Both available answers are costly
details.description: Defend the country and be treated as an apologist. Criticise it and be treated as confirming whatever the questioner already believed. Saying nothing is read as evasion.
details.energy_note: Three answers, all of them wrong.

details.aspect: It removes work as a refuge
details.description: The one place that was a functioning distraction becomes another site of the war. People take leave they cannot afford or go quiet in a way that damages their standing.
details.energy_note: Losing the only room the war was not in.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - it drives withdrawal from the host society
details.description: The predictable response is retreat into the co-national community, which is then cited as evidence of failure to integrate.
details.energy_note: Withdrawn for cause, and blamed for withdrawing.
details.notes: Direct interaction with the integration and stereotype material in assets/text/iran.

issues.title: The family who stayed, and the money
issues.category_name: Diaspora: watching it from outside
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: Remittance is not only an economic transfer. It is the mechanism by which guilt, obligation and power are negotiated inside a family split by a war.

details.aspect: The obligation has no ceiling
details.description: Whatever is sent, more is needed, because the currency keeps moving and the needs are medical. There is no amount that discharges it.
details.money_note: Annual remittance load.
details.energy_note: A bill that is never paid in full.

details.aspect: It arrives with a premium and a risk
details.description: Formal channels are closed, so the transfer goes through informal networks at a spread, with counterparty risk and legal exposure on both ends.
details.energy_note: A five percent fee and a criminal risk.

details.aspect: It sets the terms of every family conversation
details.description: The sender cannot refuse without appearing to abandon; the receiver cannot ask without appearing to demand. Both learn to talk around it, permanently.
details.energy_note: A subject the whole family talks around.

details.aspect: It delays the sender's own life by a decade
details.description: Deposit, pension, training, children - all deferred to fund a household in another country. Measured at 60, the cost of the remittance decade is not recoverable.
details.energy_note: Your thirties, spent on somebody else's survival.

issues.title: Being the nationality of a war
issues.category_name: Social fabric, stigma, and being the nationality of a war
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the next generation through silence, story, ritual and community
issues.summary: When a country is in the news as a threat, everyone carrying its nationality is reclassified abroad - at borders, at work, in the street, and by algorithms.

details.aspect: Screening intensity tracks the headlines
details.description: Secondary inspection, additional questioning and device searches rise and fall with the news cycle, which means the person's experience of a border is set by events they have no connection to.
details.energy_note: Your airport experience is set by a newspaper.

details.aspect: It reaches children at school immediately
details.description: Playground abuse follows broadcast news within days. The child has no context for it, has often never seen the country, and comes home with a question the parents have no good answer to.
details.energy_note: Explaining a war to a nine-year-old who was called a name.

details.aspect: Employment effects are real and deniable
details.description: Security clearance exclusions, export-control restrictions, and hiring hesitancy that never states its reason. Each individual decision is defensible and the aggregate is a wall.
details.energy_note: Never rejected for it. Never hired either.
details.notes: Overlaps assets/text/iran; kept here because wartime spikes are a distinct phenomenon from the baseline.

details.aspect: The stereotype is inherited by people who never lived there
details.description: Second and third generation descendants hold a name, a face and no connection, and receive the treatment anyway. Transmission here is entirely social - nothing biological is required.
details.energy_note: Inheriting a reputation you never earned.

issues.title: The community turns on itself
issues.category_name: Social fabric, stigma, and being the nationality of a war
issues.applies_to_note: Those outside the country with people inside it
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up during the event or within days
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: War splits diaspora communities along lines about the war, and the resulting fracture removes the co-ethnic support network that is the main protective factor available.

details.aspect: Suspicion of informers is not paranoia
details.description: Surveillance of diaspora communities by home-state services is documented in multiple countries. The reasonable response is caution, and caution at scale is the destruction of a community.
details.energy_note: A room where everyone is slightly careful.

details.aspect: Positions harden because the stakes are family
details.description: Political disagreement in a diaspora is not abstract - each position implies something about whose relatives deserve what. Friendships of twenty years end over it.
details.energy_note: Losing a friend over a ceasefire.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - the isolated ones fare worst
details.description: The person who withdraws from the community after a political falling-out loses their only trauma-literate social environment and is then alone in a country that does not understand any of it.
details.energy_note: Alone among people, and alone among your own.

issues.title: How it actually reaches the next generation
issues.category_name: The household as the channel it travels through
issues.applies_to_note: Children and grandchildren of the exposed, who were not there
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Outlives the person it started in
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the child through how the parent is able to parent
issues.summary: Before any genetics: the primary transmission route is a household. What the child absorbs is the parent's vigilance, silence, anger and rules, delivered daily for eighteen years.

details.aspect: The rules outlive the reason
details.description: Do not sit near a window. Always keep documents together. Never tell anyone how much you earn. Never be the last one out. These persist in households in safe countries for two generations.
details.energy_note: Air-raid habits in a suburb.

details.aspect: The silence is more transmissible than the story
details.description: Families that never discuss it produce children who know something enormous happened and have no shape for it, which is worse than the facts would have been.
details.energy_note: Growing up around an unlabelled thing.

details.aspect: Hypervigilance is taught by demonstration, not instruction
details.description: A parent who scans a restaurant on entry produces a child who scans a restaurant on entry. No one says anything and the behaviour transfers completely.
details.energy_note: Learned without a single word about it.

details.aspect: Achievement pressure as a war artefact
details.description: Everything was lost once; the only unloseable asset is a qualification in your head. So the child is pushed hard, for a reason grounded in a specific historical event they were not present at.
details.energy_note: Pushed by something that happened before you.

details.aspect: The protective factors are also transmitted
details.description: Family cohesion, ritual, humour and a coherent narrative of what happened are all documented buffers. The families that talk about it produce measurably better outcomes than the ones that do not.
details.energy_note: Talking about it is the intervention.

issues.title: Marriage, intimacy and what does not get said
issues.category_name: The household as the channel it travels through
issues.applies_to_note: Anyone physically present in a war zone
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Recurs or persists for years, manageable but not gone
issues.summary: War damage lands hardest on the relationship that is meant to be the recovery environment, and the mechanisms by which it does are almost never named in the marriage.

details.aspect: Sexual dysfunction is documented and undiscussed
details.description: Listed in the chemical-warfare survivor literature alongside depression and PTSD. It is attributed within the marriage to loss of attraction or infidelity, because the actual cause is never raised.
details.energy_note: A medical symptom read as rejection.

details.aspect: Numbness is experienced by the partner as coldness
details.description: Emotional blunting is a symptom. From the other side of the bed it is indistinguishable from having stopped caring, and it is responded to accordingly.
details.energy_note: Diagnosed by your spouse as not loving them.

details.aspect: The partner develops secondary traumatic stress
details.description: Living with and caring for a war-injured person produces measurable symptoms in the carer, who was not in the war and has no standing to claim anything.
details.energy_note: Injured by proximity, eligible for nothing.

details.aspect: SECONDARY - and it damages the economics too
details.description: The knock-on to work performance of an unaddressed intimate and marital collapse is real: concentration, ambition, risk appetite and the willingness to start anything new all fall.
details.energy_note: No business ever started, for reasons nobody will say out loud.
details.notes: Deliberate cross-link to the psychological material in assets/text/iran connecting sexual dissatisfaction to enterprise and career outcomes.

issues.title: The child who becomes the adult
issues.category_name: The household as the channel it travels through
issues.applies_to_note: Children and adolescents, whose development is running while it happens
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up months to a few years later
issues.duration_note: Does not resolve; the person adapts around it
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the child through how the parent is able to parent
issues.summary: Parentification: when the adults are incapacitated, grieving, displaced or non-speakers of the new language, a child takes over the running of the family.

details.aspect: The interpreter child
details.description: A nine-year-old translating a benefits appeal, an eviction notice or an oncology consultation. They acquire the language faster, so they acquire the responsibility, and with it the content.
details.energy_note: Told your mother's prognosis before she is.

details.aspect: The authority inversion is permanent
details.description: Once a child has managed the household's business, the parent is not restored to authority afterwards. The relationship is reorganised for life.
details.energy_note: You cannot be their child again after that.

details.aspect: It produces competence and no capacity for rest
details.description: These children are frequently high-achieving, reliable adults who cannot delegate, cannot be cared for and cannot stop. It presents at forty as burnout with no obvious cause.
details.energy_note: Extremely capable, and unable to sit down.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the appointment
details.description: She is eleven. The consultant uses the word 'palliative'. She knows what it means because she looked it up on the bus, and now she has to turn to her mother and choose a word in Farsi.
details.energy_note: Choosing the word that will tell your mother.

issues.title: Epigenetic transmission: what the evidence actually says
issues.category_name: Generational transmission: genes, methylation, and the child who was not there
issues.applies_to_note: Children and grandchildren of the exposed, who were not there
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up fifteen to forty years later, or in the next generation
issues.duration_note: Outlives the person it started in
issues.transmission_note: Carried in the regulation of genes, not the genes themselves
issues.summary: The claim that trauma is inherited biologically is partly supported, frequently overstated, and important enough to state precisely rather than loosely.

details.aspect: The FKBP5 finding
details.description: Yehuda et al. measured methylation within FKBP5 in Holocaust survivors (n=32), their adult offspring (n=22) and controls (n=8 and n=9). At bin 3 / site 6, survivors showed higher methylation than controls and their offspring showed lower; parent and offspring levels correlated significantly.
details.energy_note: A measurable mark in a child who was not there.

details.aspect: Why FKBP5 rather than any other gene
details.description: FKBP5 regulates glucocorticoid receptor sensitivity and is independently linked to PTSD and major depression - the same HPA-axis machinery implicated in the somatic and cardiovascular consequences in PTS-003.
details.energy_note: The stress thermostat, and its setting.

details.aspect: The replication, and what it narrowed the mechanism to
details.description: A 2020 American Journal of Psychiatry study replicated the decrement at intron 7 site 6 in offspring, with the effect predominating in offspring of mothers exposed in childhood - implicating maternal developmental programming rather than germline inheritance.
details.energy_note: Through the mother's own childhood, not through sperm.

details.aspect: Site specificity argues it is not noise
details.description: Offspring methylation at bin 2 / sites 3-5 was instead associated with the offspring's own childhood abuse interacting with an FKBP5 risk allele. Different sites tracked parental versus personal trauma, which is a stronger result than a single association.
details.energy_note: Two different injuries, two different sites.

details.aspect: Supporting endocrine findings from the same cohorts
details.description: Maternal age at exposure and maternal PTSD independently influence urinary cortisol in adult offspring; elevated 11beta-HSD type 2 activity in offspring; NR3C1 glucocorticoid receptor methylation differs by which parent had PTSD.
details.energy_note: Several instruments, pointing the same way.

details.aspect: HONEST LIMIT - the sample was tiny and the mechanism is contested
details.description: 32 survivors, 22 offspring, 8 and 9 controls. Critical commentary focuses on whether this supports true germline epigenetic inheritance at all, versus in-utero exposure or postnatal transmission. The replication points at the latter two.
details.energy_note: Real finding. Much smaller than the headlines.

details.aspect: What it does NOT license
details.description: It does not mean a grandchild has inherited PTSD, that an outcome is fixed, or that anyone's condition is explained by an ancestor's war. It means an altered regulatory setting on a stress-response gene, associated with vulnerability, in a specific cohort.
details.energy_note: A vulnerability, not a verdict.

issues.title: Transmission without genes at all
issues.category_name: Generational transmission: genes, methylation, and the child who was not there
issues.applies_to_note: Children and grandchildren of the exposed, who were not there
issues.war_form_note: Organised destruction of a group as a group
issues.onset_note: Shows up fifteen to forty years later, or in the next generation
issues.duration_note: Outlives the person it started in
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the next generation through silence, story, ritual and community
issues.summary: The strongest generational evidence in this dataset is not genetic. Descendants who share no ancestry with the exposed show the same elevated symptoms, which means the mechanism is the society, not the germline.

details.aspect: The Halabja three-generation design
details.description: Three cohorts - victimised as adults, victimised as children, and not affected. All three, including the unaffected, reported elevated depression, PTSD symptom severity and sleep disturbance. The cohorts were not genetically related.
details.energy_note: The unexposed cohort had it too.

details.aspect: Which means the community is the medium
details.description: Shared narrative, commemoration, economic damage, stigma, a damaged health system and a population of visibly injured adults. A child growing up inside that acquires the outcome without any biological inheritance.
details.energy_note: You catch it from the town, not the parent.

details.aspect: And it is therefore interruptible
details.description: Unlike a germline change, a social mechanism can be addressed - by services, recognition, economic repair and treatment of the exposed generation. This is the most actionable finding in the dataset.
details.energy_note: Socially transmitted means socially preventable.

details.aspect: Economic transmission is the least discussed channel
details.description: A family that lost property, savings and a breadwinner transmits that to children as reduced education, worse housing and no capital. The mental health outcome follows from the economics without anything mystical.
details.energy_note: Inherited poverty, wearing a psychiatric label.

issues.title: What descendants actually carry
issues.category_name: Generational transmission: genes, methylation, and the child who was not there
issues.applies_to_note: Children and grandchildren of the exposed, who were not there
issues.war_form_note: The peace afterwards, which is not the end of the effect
issues.onset_note: Shows up fifteen to forty years later, or in the next generation
issues.duration_note: Outlives the person it started in
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the next generation through silence, story, ritual and community
issues.summary: The third generation is not a study population. They are people who have particular recurring experiences - and those experiences are specific enough to be listed rather than gestured at.

details.aspect: A grief with no memory attached
details.description: Strong feeling about an event they cannot remember, which is socially illegitimate - they know they have no right to it, and they have it anyway.
details.energy_note: Mourning something you never saw.

details.aspect: Being the repository
details.description: The grandchild who gets told the story the children were never told, usually once, usually late, usually with an instruction not to upset anyone.
details.energy_note: Handed the whole thing at twenty-three, alone.

details.aspect: Obligation to succeed on behalf of the dead
details.description: The achievement is framed as vindication of people who did not survive. That is a heavy engine and it does not have an off switch.
details.energy_note: A career as a memorial.

details.aspect: The identity is inherited whether or not it is wanted
details.description: Some descendants organise their lives around it; others refuse it entirely. Both are responses to something they did not choose, and the refusal costs as much effort as the embrace.
details.energy_note: Opting out is also a full-time position.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the family name
details.description: She is 26, born in Hamburg, and does not speak the language. A man at a party hears her surname and asks about a war that ended before her mother was born. She does not know the answer and feels, precisely, like a fraud.
details.energy_note: Interrogated about a war you have no memory of.

issues.title: Physical inheritance: the parent's damaged body
issues.category_name: Generational transmission: genes, methylation, and the child who was not there
issues.applies_to_note: Children and grandchildren of the exposed, who were not there
issues.war_form_note: Chemical and other prohibited weapons
issues.onset_note: Shows up fifteen to forty years later, or in the next generation
issues.duration_note: Outlives the person it started in
issues.transmission_note: Reaches the next generation through the parent's damaged body
issues.summary: Some of the generational transfer is neither psychological nor epigenetic. It is that a chemically or radiologically injured parent has children, and the injury is present in the pregnancy.

details.aspect: Infertility, miscarriage and congenital abnormality
details.description: Documented at higher rates in sulfur-mustard-exposed populations, alongside cancer. For the exposed parent each pregnancy is a source of dread rather than anticipation.
details.energy_note: Every pregnancy as a test of what was done to you.

details.aspect: The decision whether to have children at all
details.description: Exposed survivors face a choice nobody else faces: whether their exposure makes parenthood irresponsible. There is rarely any genetic counselling available to inform it.
details.energy_note: Deciding about a child on no information.

details.aspect: A disabled child, in a system with nothing for them
details.description: Where the outcome does occur, the family faces lifelong care in a place with no specialist services and a sanctioned supply chain for equipment.
details.energy_note: The war, delivered to a child, in 2026.

details.aspect: Attribution is impossible and the family does it anyway
details.description: No mechanism exists to establish whether a given birth defect came from a given exposure. The parents assign the cause themselves, and carry it, without any way to be right or wrong.
details.energy_note: Guilty of something nobody can confirm.
